sections.title: Ancient Burial Sites
sections.html:
1. Ancient Burial Sites is played before the first agenda is revealed.
  2. A player with zero cultural planets may be chosen.

sections.title: Archaeological Expedition
sections.html: 1. A player must control at least one planet with a trait to play and resolve Archaeological Expedition.

sections.title: Assassinate Representative
sections.html: 1. The chosen player may still play rider cards or use other abilities.

sections.title: Blitz
sections.html: 1. If the L1Z1X player plays Blitz, they may use the gained Bombardment ability of each of their non–fighter ships in the system when resolving their Harrow faction ability during that invasion.

sections.title: Bribery
sections.html:
1. Bribery may be played after the speaker has abstained, or would vote if they are unable to.
  2. A player may spend zero trade goods when they play Bribery.
  3. A player must have cast votes for an outcome to play Bribery, and the additional votes must be cast for the same outcome.
    1. If the Argent player is speaker, only they can play Bribery, and must do so immediately after they cast votes.
  4. The speaker may play Distinguished Councilor after another player plays Bribery.
  5. Bribery is played before any effects that change the outcome of an agenda.

sections.title: Brilliance
sections.html: 1. A player may choose themself as the player who gains their breakthrough.

sections.title: Bunker
sections.html:
1. The modifier will apply to bombardment rolls for each planet in the active system.
  2. The modifier will apply to bombardment rolls made for the L1Z1X player’s Harrow faction ability during that invasion.

sections.title: Confounding Legal Text
sections.html:
1. Any predictions made on the outcome of the agenda resolve based on the newly elected player.
  2. Confounding Legal Text is played after any effects that allow a player to cast additional votes.
  3. Confounding Legal Text is played before Deadly Plot is played, before revealing the hidden agenda for the Covert Legislation agenda, and before the Drive the Debate objective may be scored. 4. Confounding Legal Text may be played after Confusing Legal Text is played.

sections.title: Confusing Legal Text
sections.html:
1. Any predictions made on the outcome of the agenda resolve based on the newly elected player.
  2. Confusing Legal Text is played after any effects that allow a player to cast additional votes.
  3. Confusing Legal Text is played before Deadly Plot is played, before revealing the hidden agenda for the Covert Legislation agenda, and before the Drive the Debate objective may be scored. 4. Confusing Legal Text may be played after Confounding Legal Text is played.

sections.title: Construction Rider
sections.html:
1. After playing a Construction Rider, a player may use additional abilities, including playing other rider cards.
    1. Any other riders may be played to predict the same or a different outcome.
  2. The effect of a successful Construction Rider will be resolved after the effect of the agenda.
  3. A player who cannot vote may still play a Construction Rider.
  4. If a player wishes to place a space dock, but there are none left in their reinforcements, they may remove a space dock from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead.
  5. The Saar player may play a Construction Rider, and may place a space dock in a system containing a planet they control if successful.
  6. If a player successfully resolves a Construction Rider while they own the Minister of Industry law, they use the Production ability of their units in the system where they place their space dock. They may exhaust planets for resources, but those planets cannot be used to cast votes for the remainder of the agenda phase.

sections.title: Coup D’etat
sections.html: 1. The active player may still use any “at the end of your turn” abilities.

sections.title: Courageous to the End
sections.html:
1. Any combat roll modifiers will not apply to the dice roll for Courageous to the End.
  2. Effects that cancel hits, such as Sustain Damage, cannot be used to prevent ships from being destroyed.

sections.title: Cripple Defenses
sections.html: 1. The chosen planet may have zero PDS on it.

sections.title: Crisis
sections.html: 1. Crisis will skip the turn of the next unpassed player.

sections.title: Deadly Plot
sections.html:
1. Any prediction made for a rider or similar ability is incorrect, and will not resolve.
  2. A player cannot make the prediction that Deadly Plot will be played when they predict the outcome of an agenda.
  3. Deadly Plot is played after any effects that allow a player to cast additional votes, and after any effects that change the outcome of an agenda.
  4. Deadly Plot is played before revealing the hidden agenda for the Covert Legislation agenda, and before the Drive the Debate objective may be scored. 5. If a player predicts multiple outcomes, they may play Deadly Plot regardless of which outcome would be resolved.
    1. If the Xxcha player uses their commander, Elder Qanoj, to vote for one outcome, when they have predicted another, they may play Deadly Plot regardless of which outcome would be resolved.

sections.title: Decoy Operation
sections.html: 1. If a mech is damaged when it is removed, it will remain damaged when it is placed.

sections.title: Diplomacy Rider
sections.html:
1. The Mecatol Rex system may be chosen.
  2. After playing a Diplomacy Rider, a player may use additional abilities, including playing other rider cards.
    1. Any other riders may be played to predict the same or a different outcome.
  3. The effect of a successful Diplomacy Rider will be resolved after the effect of the agenda.
  4. A player who cannot vote may still play a Diplomacy Rider.

sections.title: Diplomatic Pressure
sections.html:
1. The target player chooses which promissory note they give.
  2. Giving a promissory note because of Diplomatic Pressure is not resolving a transaction.
  3. A player cannot play a second Diplomatic Pressure targeting the same player during the same agenda.
    1. A player may play a second Diplomatic Pressure targeting a different player during the same agenda.
    2. Another player may play a second Diplomatic Pressure targeting the same player during the same agenda.
    3. A player may play a second Diplomatic Pressure targeting the same player during a later agenda.

sections.title: Direct Hit
sections.html:
1. If multiple ships use their Sustain Damage ability, a Direct Hit may be played for each.
  2. A Direct Hit may be used whenever hits produced by a player’s units or abilities are cancelled by a ship using its Sustain Damage ability.
  3. When a player uses the Sustain Damage ability of one of their ships, they do not have to decide if another of their ships in the same combat will use its Sustain Damage ability until after their opponent has used or declined to use a Direct Hit.
  4. When Direct Hit is used outside of combat, if used on a ship with capacity, then fighters and/or ground forces must immediately be removed from the space area to meet the capacity limit.
    1. For example, say a player has a dreadnought, a destroyer and a fighter in a system with no other ships during the Space Cannon Defense step. During the Roll Dice step, two hits are produced against that player. They cancel one with the dreadnought’s Sustain Damage ability, but a Direct Hit is played to destroy it. The fighter in that system is immediately removed. The player must then assign the other produced hit to their destroyer.
  5. A mech cannot be destroyed by Direct Hit, unless a game effect causes the mech to be considered a ship.

sections.title: Disable
sections.html:
1. If the Ul player is targeted, their Hel–Titans will still participate in the ground combat during the current invasion.
  2. If Disable results in no units on a planet having the Planetary Shield ability, then the ability of the Magen Defense Grid technology cannot be used during ground combat on that planet during that invasion.
    1. Disable has no effect on the Magen Defense Grid Ω or Magen Defense Grid ΩΩ technologies.
  3. Disable does not affect the Space Cannon Offense step, and is not played until the start of the Invasion step.

sections.title: Distinguished Councilor
sections.html:
1. A player must have cast votes for an outcome to play Distinguished Councilor, and the additional votes must be cast for the same outcome.
  2. A player may only play Distinguished Councilor after their normal vote, not after they cast additional votes at another point.
  3. The speaker may play Distinguished Councilor after another player plays Bribery.
  4. Distinguished Councilor is played before any effects that change the outcome of an agenda.

sections.title: Divert Funding
sections.html:
1. A player must have at least one non–unit upgrade, non–faction technology to play and resolve Divert Funding.
  2. A player must still meet the prerequisites for the technology they research.
    1. The returned technology does not count towards meeting the prerequisites.
  3. The researched technology may be a unit upgrade technology, and it may be a faction technology.
  4. The researched technology cannot be the returned technology.
  5. Other players must decide whether to play Sabotage, or otherwise cancel the action card, before the player playing Divert Funding announces which technology they are researching.
  6. If a player later gains the technology they returned, they gain it readied.
  7. If the player returns the Antimass Deflectors technology, their units may remain in and move out of any asteroid fields they are currently in, but cannot move additional units into or through.

sections.title: Economic Initiative
sections.html: 1. A player with zero cultural planets may play Economic Initiative.

sections.title: Emergency Repairs
sections.html: 1. A player may play Emergency Repairs at the start of the first round of combat to repair ships damaged in a previous combat, or during the Space Cannon Offense step of the current action.

sections.title: Exchange Program
sections.html: 1. The player who played Exchange Program does not have to agree to place the infantry.

sections.title: Experimental Battlestation
sections.html:
1. The selected space dock will use the Space Cannon ability during the Space Cannon Offense step of the current tactical action.
  2. Hits may only be assigned to the active player’s ships.
  3. Experimental Battlestation cannot be played if no ships are moved into the active system, even if the active player already has ships in that system.
    1. If ships are moved into the active system, ships that were already in that system may be assigned any hits produced.
    2. If a ship is moved out of the active system and then back in, Experimental Battlestation may be played.
    3. If all moving ships are lost to a gravity rift, and none arrive in the active system, Experimental Battlestation cannot be played.
  4. Experimental Battlestation cannot be played if ships are moved outside of the Move Ships step, such as during a retreat, or while resolving the Mahact player’s Benediction hero ability.
  5. The hits produced by the Experimental Battlestation space cannon rolls may be cancelled with Maneuvering Jets.

sections.title: Exploration Probe
sections.html: 1. A player must have an exploration token in or adjacent to a system containing one or more of their ships to play and resolve Exploration Probe.

sections.title: Extreme Duress
sections.html:
1. If that player has the ability to perform multiple actions in a turn, their first action must be a strategic action to avoid the penalty.
  2. If a player has multiple strategy cards, at least one of them needs to be readied to target them with Extreme Duress
    1. If they have multiple readied, they may perform a strategic action with any to avoid the penalty.

sections.title: Fighter Conscription
sections.html:
1. Only one fighter will be placed in a system containing both a space dock and a ship with capacity.
  2. A player may place a fighter in a system that is at its capacity limit. If they do so, they must then remove a fighter or ground force from the space area of that system.

sections.title: Fire Team
sections.html: 1. Any modifiers on the original combat roll will apply to the reroll.

sections.title: Flank Speed
sections.html:
1. A second Flank Speed cannot be played to give +2 to the move value of each ship.
  2. Cancelling Flank Speed will not cancel the system activation.

sections.title: Focused Research
sections.html:
1. A player cannot play Focused Research if they have less than four trade goods.
  2. A player must still meet the prerequisites for the technology they research.
  3. Other players must decide whether to play Sabotage, or otherwise cancel the action card, before the player playing Focused Research announces which technology they are researching.

sections.title: Frontline Deployment
sections.html:
1. A player must control at least one planet to play and resolve Frontline Deployment.
  2. All three infantry must be placed on a single planet.

sections.title: Ghost Ship
sections.html:
1. A player may place the destroyer in the Creuss gate (tile 17), the wormhole nexus, or any system with a printed wormhole or wormhole token.
    1. Placing the destroyer in the inactive wormhole nexus will cause it to flip to its active side.
  2. The destroyer cannot be placed in the home system of an eliminated player.
  3. There must be an eligible system to place the destroyer in for a player to play and resolve Ghost Ship.
  4. If a player wishes to place a destroyer, but there are none left in their reinforcements, they may remove a destroyer from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead.

sections.title: Ghost Squad
sections.html:
1. Ghost Squad is played after the active player has assigned which planet each of their ground forces are being committed to. They cannot modify this after Ghost Squad has been played.
  2. Ghost Squad may be played whenever ground forces are committed, such as from the Yin player’s Quantum Dissemination Ω hero ability.
    1. Ghost Squad cannot be played in response to abilities that place ground forces on a planet without committing them, such as the Colonial Redistribution agenda.
  3. The Ul player cannot use Ghost Squad to move a Hel–Titan.
  4. A player may move zero ground forces with Ghost Squad.

sections.title: Hack Election
sections.html:
1. The speaker will still vote last.
  2. The Argent player will still vote before all other players.

sections.title: Hack Election Ω
sections.html:
1. Hack Election Ω will not allow a player to vote if another game effect would prevent them from doing so.
  2. The speaker votes before the player that played Hack Election Ω.
    1. Players will play Bribery after the speaker votes. The player that played Hack Election Ω cannot play Bribery.
  3. If the Argent player plays Hack Election Ω, they will vote last.

sections.title: Harness Energy
sections.html: 1. If a player has their maximum number of commodities, they may still play Harness Energy. If they do, they will still trigger any “when [this] player replenishes commodities” effects, most notably the Trade Agreement promissory note.

sections.title: Imperial Rider
sections.html:
1. After playing an Imperial Rider, a player may use additional abilities, including playing other rider cards.
    1. Any other riders may be played to predict the same or a different outcome.
  2. The effect of a successful Imperial Rider will be resolved after the effect of the agenda.
  3. A player who cannot vote may still play an Imperial Rider.

sections.title: Impersonation
sections.html:
1. A player cannot play Impersonation if they have less than three influence available.
  2. A player with three secret objectives may draw a fourth, and then shuffle one of their unscored secret objectives into the secret objective deck.
    1. If a player has scored three secret objectives, they may use Impersonation to draw a secret objective, then immediately shuffle it into the secret objective deck.

sections.title: In The Silence Of Space
sections.html: 1. Only the ships in the chosen system may move through systems that contain other players’ ships. Ships in other systems may still move to the active system if they are able to do so without moving through systems that contain other players’ ships.

sections.title: Industrial Initiative
sections.html: 1. A player with zero industrial planets may play Industrial Initiative.

sections.title: Infiltrate
sections.html:
1. If the L1Z1X player plays Infiltrate before they resolve their Assimilate ability, or vice versa, they will replace zero PDS and space docks with zero PDS and space docks when they resolve the latter ability.
  2. If a player wishes to place a structure, but there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, they may remove a structure of that type from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. That player may make the choice for each structure.
    1. The Ul player will place each of their Hel Titan PDS undamaged.

sections.title: Insubordination
sections.html: 1. Insubordination cannot target a player with zero command tokens in their tactic pool.

sections.title: Intercept
sections.html:
1. During the next round of combat, the targeted player may declare another retreat.
  2. Intercept cannot be played to prevent Skilled Retreat or the Naalu player’s Foresight faction ability.

sections.title: Leadership Rider
sections.html:
1. After playing a Leadership Rider, a player may use additional abilities, including playing other rider cards.
    1. Any other riders may be played to predict the same or a different outcome.
  2. The effect of a successful Leadership Rider will be resolved after the effect of the agenda.
  3. A player who cannot vote may still play a Leadership Rider.

sections.title: Lost Star Chart
sections.html:
1. If the Enforced Travel Ban law is in play, Lost Star Chart will allow a player to move through wormholes during this action.
    1. A player may move from a system containing an alpha wormhole to a system containing an alpha wormhole, and similarly for beta wormholes.
  2. If the active system contains a beta wormhole, a player that has a unit with the Deep Space Cannon ability in an alpha wormhole may produce hits against ships in the active system during the Space Cannon Offense step of the tactical action, and vice versa.
  3. A player may retreat from a system containing an alpha wormhole into a system containing a beta wormhole, and vice versa, during this action.
  4. If a player has units or controls planets in a system with an alpha wormhole, and another player has units or controls planets in a system with a beta wormhole, then those two players are neighbors during this action.
    1. The Mentak player may use their Pillage ability against a player in this manner.
  5. A player moving a ship between two systems, both with alpha wormholes or both with beta wormholes, does not have to move through the wormhole, as the systems are adjacent. In particular, if one of those systems has the Ion Storm token, that player chooses if the Ion Storm token will flip.

sections.title: Lucky Shot
sections.html:
1. A player cannot use Lucky Shot against their own units.
  2. Effects that cancel hits, such as Sustain Damage, cannot be used to prevent ships from being destroyed.

sections.title: Maneuvering Jets
sections.html:
1. Maneuvering Jets cannot be used to cancel hits during combat.
  2. Maneuvering Jets may cancel hits produced during either the Space Cannon Offense or the Space Cannon Defense step.
  3. A player cannot play a second Maneuvering Jets to cancel a second hit produced by the same Space Cannon roll.
    1. During the Space Cannon Offense step, each player makes their Space Cannon roll independent of each other player, in clockwise order. As such, a player may use one Maneuvering Jets after each other player makes a space cannon roll.
    2. During the Space Cannon Defense step, the units on each planet make their Space Cannon roll independent of the units on each other planet. The active player chooses the order. As such, a player may use one Maneuvering Jets for each planet they are committing ground forces to.
  4. Maneuvering Jets may cancel hits produced due to the Experimental Battlestation action card.

sections.title: Manipulate Investments
sections.html:
1. If a player still has a strategy card because of Political Stability, trade goods may be placed on that strategy card. However, those trade goods will remain on that strategy card until it is chosen from the common area.
    1. If a player takes the strategy card with trade goods on it from the player who played Political Stability, using the ability of the Imperial Arbiter law or similar, they will not gain the trade goods, which will remain on the strategy card.

sections.title: Master Plan
sections.html:
1. Effects that trigger at the start or end of a player’s turn will not trigger between each of those player’s actions.
  2. If a player’s turn is ended by a game effect, they cannot use Master Plan to perform an additional action.
  3. A player cannot use Master Plan to pass on the same turn they performed an action.
  4. If a player’s second action would be to use a component action to play an action card, and that card is cancelled, they are not required to perform an alternate second action on that turn.

sections.title: Mercenary Contract
sections.html:
1. When a planet card is returned to the planet card deck, the player that previously controlled it will no longer do so. They remove their control token from the planet.
  2. If the planet card is returned to the planet card deck, then when a player later gains control of that planet, they will explore it.
    1. The planet will not be explored if it does not have a trait. If the planet is in The Fracture, however, the gaining player will draw a relic.
  3. If the Mecatol Rex planet card is returned to the planet card deck, the custodians token is not replaced. A player will be able to later commit ground forces without paying influence, and without gaining a victory point.4. 5. If a legendary planet card is returned to the planet card deck, the player that controlled it also loses the associated legendary planet ability card.

sections.title: Mining Initiative
sections.html:
1. A player must control at least one planet to play and resolve Mining Initiative.
  2. Mining Initiative does not exhaust the chosen planet.

sections.title: Morale Boost
sections.html:
1. The +1 will apply to any rerolls during the combat round.
  2. A second Morale Boost cannot be played during a combat round to give +2 to the combat rolls of a player’s units.
  3. Morale Boost has no effect on anti–fighter barrage rolls.

sections.title: Nav Suite
sections.html:
1. Wormholes are not anomalies.
  2. An anomaly will retain its regular effect if a player retreats.
  3. A player may move ships through or into an asteroid field without the Antimass Deflectors technology. After moving into, those ships may remain there and move out during a later action without harm.
  4. A player may move ships through or out of a gravity rift without rolling for removal. Those ships will not get +1 to their move value.
  5. A player may move ships through a nebula. Ships moving out of a nebula retain their normal move value.
  6. A player may move ships through or into a supernova. After moving into, those ships may remain there and move out during a later action without harm.
  7. Other players cannot ignore the effect of anomalies during this tactical action.
    1. The Naalu player will still be affected by anomalies if they use their Foresight faction ability.

sections.title: Overrule
sections.html: 1. If a player is eliminated, the strategy cards that they had are considered “unchosen”.

sections.title: Parley
sections.html:
1. If a player commits ground forces to multiple planets, Parley will affect ground forces on only one planet.
  2. The returned ground forces cannot be committed to another planet during the same tactical action.

sections.title: Plagiarize
sections.html:
1. A player cannot play Plagiarize if they have less than five influence available.
  2. A player does not need to meet the prerequisites of the technology they gain from Plagiarize.
  3. The active player must announce which technology they are gaining before other players decide whether to play a Sabotage, or otherwise cancel the action card.
  4. If a faction has a faction–specific unit upgrade as one of their faction technologies, they cannot use Plagiarize to gain that unit upgrade.
    1. If a player’s neighbor owns a faction–specific unit upgrade, it cannot be chosen in order to gain the generic version of that unit upgrade by using Plagiarize.

sections.title: Plague
sections.html: 1. A planet with zero infantry on it may be targeted by Plague.

sections.title: Political Stability
sections.html:
1. During the upcoming agenda phase, all abilities stay resolved in speaker order, not initiative order.
  2. The strategy cards are readied when Political Stability is played.
  3. The “Return Strategy Cards” step is the last step of the status phase. All other steps must be completed by all players before Political Stability may be played. This includes scoring and revealing objectives, drawing action cards (and discarding down to hand limit, if necessary), and gaining and redistributing command tokens.
    1. If a player draws Political Stability during the status phase, they may play it during the same phase.

sections.title: Politics Rider
sections.html:
1. After playing a Politics Rider, a player may use additional abilities, including playing other rider cards.
    1. Any other riders may be played to predict the same or a different outcome.
  2. The effect of a successful Politics Rider will be resolved after the effect of the agenda.
  3. A player who cannot vote may still play a Politics Rider.

sections.title: Public Disgrace
sections.html:
1. If the originally chosen strategy card has trade goods on it, those will not be taken if Public Disgrace is played.
  2. Public Disgrace may only be played during the regular choosing of a strategy card during the strategy phase. It cannot be played when other effects cause a player to take a strategy card, such as the Imperial Arbiter agenda.

sections.title: Puppets On A String
sections.html:
1. The player who played Puppets On A String is considered the active player during their action.
  2. It is not considered the turn of the player who played Puppets On A String for game effects.
    1. They cannot use any “at the start/end of your turn” abilities.
    2. If the Yssaril player plays Puppets On A String, and owns their Transparasteel Plating faction technology, passed players may still play action cards during the action.
  3. The active player may use any “before/after you perform an action” abilities.
  4. Abilities that would end the active player’s turn instead end their action.
  5. The active player cannot use the Fleet Logistics technology to perform an additional action.
    1. The active player may use the Master Plan action card or the Minister of War agenda to perform an additional action.
    2. If the active player performs a component action, they may then use the ability of Suffi An, the Keleres commander, to perform additional actions.
  6. The active player is still considered passed during their action. They do not pass at the end of the action.
    1. The active player cannot score the Prove Endurance secret objective at the end of their action.

sections.title: Reactor Meltdown
sections.html:
1. A player cannot destroy their own space dock with Reactor Meltdown.
  2. At least one space dock belonging to another player must exist on the game board in a non–home system for a player to play and resolve Reactor Meltdown.
  3. If a player owns a space dock in another player’s home system, that space dock cannot be targeted by Reactor Meltdown.
    1. A space dock in an eliminated player’s home system cannot be targeted.

sections.title: Refit Troops
sections.html:
1. A player must have at least one infantry on the game board to play and resolve Refit Troops.
  2. If a player has no mechs left in their reinforcements, they may remove a mech from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. The mech will be placed undamaged.

sections.title: Reflective Shielding
sections.html:
1. If Reflective Shielding is played after a ship uses its Sustain Damage ability during an Assign Hits step, then the hits produced by Reflective Shielding are added to any other hits produced in the immediately proceeding Roll Dice step.
    1. A unit that used its Sustain Damage ability to cancel some of those other hits, and been repaired, cannot use its Sustain Damage ability again to cancel the hits produced by Reflective Shielding.
  2. If Reflective Shielding is played after a ship uses its Sustain Damage ability at any other time during combat (for example, when the Creuss player uses their Dimensional Splicer faction technology ability), the hits are assigned immediately.

sections.title: Reparations
sections.html:
1. Reparations may be played by a player with no exhausted planets, or when they lose control of a planet to a player with no readied planets.
    1. Reparations cannot be played by a player with no exhausted planets when they lose control of a planet to a player with no readied planets.

sections.title: Repeal Law
sections.html: 1. There must be at least one law in play for a player to play and resolve Repeal Law.

sections.title: Rescue
sections.html: 1. If the chosen ship is in a gravity rift, it must roll for removal.

sections.title: Reveal Prototype
sections.html:
1. A player must still meet the prerequisites for the technology they research.
  2. A player cannot play Reveal Prototype if they have less than four resources available.
  3. A player cannot play Reveal Prototype if they already own the unit upgrade technology for each unit they have in the combat.
  4. Other players must decide whether to play Sabotage, or otherwise cancel the action card, before the player playing Reveal Prototype announces which technology they are researching.

sections.title: Reverse Engineer
sections.html:
1. Reverse Engineer may be played if the action card is discarded after being played or cancelled, if it is discarded due to hand size limits, or if it is discarded for another game effect.
  2. It is public knowlege which action cards a player takes using Reverse Engineer.

sections.title: Rise of a Messiah
sections.html: 1. A player that controls zero planets may play Rise of a Messiah.

sections.title: Rout
sections.html:
1. A player cannot announce a retreat if there is not at least one eligible system to retreat to.
  2. A player cannot announce a retreat from the space combat initiated by the Mahact player’s Benediction hero ability.

sections.title: Sabotage
sections.html:
1. If a player has a second copy of an action card, they may play it if the first was cancelled by Sabotage.
  2. If an action card is cancelled by Sabotage, no costs are paid.
  3. A player playing an action card announces the following before Sabotage may be played:
    1. Any targeted planets, system, units, players, cards, outcomes, and/or other such objects.
    2. The value of any variable cost to be paid.
  4. Any dice are rolled and any cards are drawn only after all other players has declined to play Sabotage.
  5. If an action card instructs a player to research a technology, that player need not announce what technology they are researching until all other players has declined to play Sabotage.
  6. If an action card is played that will have an effect later, such as a rider, that card may only be cancelled by Sabotage when it is originally played.
  7. If the action card that was cancelled by Sabotage was to be used to perform a component action, the active player must perform a different action, or pass.
    1. If the component action was to be the second action the active player was to perform on their turn, through an effect such as the Fleet Logistics technology, the active player may end their turn without performing a second action and without passing.

sections.title: Salvage
sections.html: 1. The active player may perform transactions after Salvage is played and before it resolves.

sections.title: Sanction
sections.html:
1. After playing a Sanction, a player may use additional abilities, including playing rider cards.
    1. Any riders may be played to predict the same or a different outcome.
  2. The effect of a successful Sanction will be resolved after the effect of the agenda.
  3. A player who cannot vote may still play a Sanction.

sections.title: Scuttle
sections.html: 1. A player must have at least one non–fighter ship on the game board to play and resolve Scuttle.

sections.title: Seize Artifact
sections.html: 1. A player must have at least one neighbor with at least one relic fragment to play and resolve Seize Artifact.

sections.title: Shields Holding
sections.html:
1. Shields Holding cannot be used to cancel hits produced by Space Cannon abilities.
  2. Shields Holding cannot be used to prevent an effect that directly destroys a unit.
  3. Shields Holding cannot be used during ground combat.
  4. Shields Holding may be used to cancel hits produced by any ability during space combat.
    1. Shields Holding may be used to cancel hits produced by an anti–fighter barrage roll.
  5. A player cannot play a second Shields Holding to cancel a second pair of hits produced by the same dice roll or other source.

sections.title: Signal Jamming
sections.html:
1. The Mecatol Rex system may be chosen.
  2. A command token cannot be placed in an eliminated player’s home system.

sections.title: Skilled Retreat
sections.html:
1. Using Skilled Retreat is not a retreat. As such, it cannot be cancelled with the Intercept action card.
  2. A player may use Skilled Retreat to move into a system that does not contain their ships, as long as it does not contain another player’s ships.
  3. A player cannot use Skilled Retreat to move into a nebula.
  4. Fighters are moved without being transported. Ground forces may be transported.
  5. After moving, capacity and fleet pool limits apply in the destination system.
  6. If the destination system already contains a player’s command token, no command token is placed.
  7. If a player has no command tokens in their reinforcements, they must take one from any pool of their command sheet and place that instead.

sections.title: Solar Flare
sections.html:
1. The active player may still use the Space Cannon ability of their units.
  2. During the Space Cannon Defense step of an invasion during the same tactical action, other players may use the Space Cannon ability of their units.
  3. Another player cannot play Experimental Battlestation during this tactical action.

sections.title: Spy
sections.html:
1. Spy cannot target a player with zero action cards in their hand.
  2. If the targeted player has Reverse Engineer in their hand, they must first give a random action card to the player who played Spy. Only if the card they gave was not Reverse Engineer may then then play it to take Spy into their hand from the discard pile.

sections.title: Strategize
sections.html:
1. If a player is eliminated, the strategy cards that they had are considered “unchosen”.
  2. The active player must still spend a command token to perform the secondary ability, other than for Leadership.

sections.title: Tactical Bombardment
sections.html:
1. A player must have at least one unit with the Bombardment ability to play and resolve Tactical Bombardment.
  2. A player may select a system that contains zero readied planets controlled by other players.

sections.title: Technology Rider
sections.html:
1. After playing a Technology Rider, a player may use additional abilities, including playing other rider cards.
    1. Any other riders may be played to predict the same or a different outcome.
  2. The effect of a successful Technology Rider will be resolved after the effect of the agenda.
  3. A player who cannot vote may still play a Technology Rider.
  4. A player must still meet the prerequisites for the technology they research.
    1. A player may exhaust a planet with a technology specialty to ignore a prerequisite on a technology as normal. This planet will ready at the end of the agenda phase.
    2. A player may exhaust the AI Development Algorithm technology to ignore a prerequisite on a unit upgrade technology as normal. AI Development Algorithm will not ready at the end of the agenda phase.

sections.title: Trade Rider
sections.html:
1. After playing a Trade Rider, a player may use additional abilities, including playing other rider cards.
    1. Any other riders may be played to predict the same or a different outcome.
  2. The effect of a successful Trade Rider will be resolved after the effect of the agenda.
  3. A player who cannot vote may still play a Trade Rider.

sections.title: Unexpected Action
sections.html: 1. Unexpected Action cannot be played by a player with zero command tokens on the game board.

sections.title: Unstable Planet
sections.html:
1. A player may select an exhausted planet, and they may select a planet with fewer than three infantry on it (including zero).
  2. If the selected planet has three or fewer infantry on it, all infantry will be destroyed. Otherwise, three infantry will be destroyed.

sections.title: Upgrade
sections.html:
1. The cruiser must be in the system when it is activated for Upgrade to be played. Upgrade cannot be played if the cruiser is moved into the active system later in the turn.
  2. A player must have at least one cruiser in the active system to play and resolve Upgrade.
  3. If a player wishes to place a dreadnought, but there are none left in their reinforcements, they may remove a dreadnought from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. This dreadnought will be placed undamaged.

sections.title: Uprising
sections.html:
1. Uprising cannot be played if all planets owned by each other player is exhausted.
  2. Uprising cannot target an exhausted planet.

sections.title: Veto
sections.html:
1. Veto, the Xxcha Quash faction ability, the Xxcha Political Favor promissory note, and the Political Secret promissory note are all played in the same timing window, before the rider timing window.
    1. If Veto is used after any Political Secret promissory notes have been played, those are immediately returned and will have no effect on the replacement agenda.
  2. Each agenda is considered separate for the purpose of limiting each pair of players to one transaction per agenda.
  3. A second Veto may be used on the replacement agenda.

sections.title: War Effort
sections.html: 1. If a player wishes to place a cruiser, but there are none left in their reinforcements, they may remove a cruiser from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. This cruiser will be placed undamaged.

sections.title: War Machine
sections.html:
1. A second War Machine cannot be played during use of production to give +8 to the total production value and/or to reduce the combined cost of the produced units by 2.
  2. War Machine may only be used by effects that cause a unit to use its Production ability. It cannot be used for other effects that produce units.

sections.title: Warfare Rider
sections.html:
1. After playing a Warfare Rider, a player may use additional abilities, including playing other rider cards.
    1. Any other riders may be played to predict the same or a different outcome.
  2. The effect of a successful Warfare Rider will be resolved after the effect of the agenda.
  3. A player who cannot vote may still play a Warfare Rider.
  4. If a player wishes to place a dreadnought, but there are none in their reinforcements, they may remove a dreadnought from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. This dreadnought will be placed undamaged.

sections.title: Waylay
sections.html: 1. A ship with the Sustain Damage ability may cancel a hit produced by an anti–fighter barrage roll if Waylay causes that ship to be eligible to be hit.

sections.title: Anti–Intellectual Revolution
sections.html:
1. When Anti–Intellectual Revolution is a law in play, a player that directly gains a technology will be unaffected.
    1. The Nekro player is never affected by the Anti–Intellectual Revolution law.
  2. The Nekro player’s Valefar Assimilator technologies count for the “Against” effect, whether their tokens are on another player’s faction technology or not.
  3. A player with no non–fighter ships on the game board may still research technology when Anti–Intellectual Revolution is a law in play.
  4. A player may only exhaust planets they control for the “Against” effect of Anti–Intellectual Revolution.

sections.title: Archived Secret
sections.html:
1. A player with three scored secret objectives may draw a fourth. However, they must immediately shuffle it into the secret objective deck.
  2. If a player draws the Drive the Debate secret objective while resolving Archived Secret, they cannot score it immediately.

sections.title: Checks and Balances
sections.html:
1. If there are any trade goods on a chosen strategy card while Checks and Balances is a law in play, the player who chose the strategy card gains them, not the player who receives that card.
  2. The Public Disgrace action card may be played after a player has chosen a strategy card and announced which player will be receiving it. The player must choose a different strategy card, and then choose the same or a different player to receive it.

sections.title: Clandestine Operations
sections.html: 1. If the “For” effect of Clandestine Operations is resolved, the removed tokens may be from any pool or pools on a player’s command sheet.

sections.title: Classified Document Leaks
sections.html:
1. If Classified Document Leaks is revealed when only one secret objective is in play, players may only vote for that secret objective or abstain. If no votes are cast, the speaker must decide for that secret objective to be elected.
    1. Players may still play riders if only one secret objective has been scored.
  2. The player that originally owned the secret objective elected by Classified Document Leaks cannot score it again after it becomes a public objective.
  3. The elected secret objective no longer counts towards the original player’s limit of three secret objectives.
  4. If Classified Document Leaks is discarded, the elected secret objective is not returned to the original player, and it is no longer scorable as a public objective. It remains in play, not discarded.
  5. A player can score a maximum of one objective of any type during or after each combat. A player cannot score the elected objective and one of their own secret objectives from the same combat.
  6. The elected objective becomes a public objective and stops being a secret objective.
    1. If Classified Document Leaks is elected by Miscount Disclosed, the objective that was originally elected will remain a public objective during the vote. It therefore cannot be re–elected.
    2. If there are no other secret objectives eligable to be elected by the Miscount Disclosed revote, Classified Document Leaks will be discarded, and another agenda will be revealed and voted on.

sections.title: Colonial Redistribution
sections.html:
1. If the player that originally controlled the elected planet has the fewest victory points, they may choose themselves to place an infantry on that planet.
  2. If the elected planet has the Demilitarized Zone exploration card attached, no infantry will be placed on it. Control of the planet will remain with the original player.

sections.title: Committee Formation
sections.html:
1. Committee Formation is resolved after any riders have been played, if the owner so chooses. Riders will resolve if the predicted outcome matches the player elected by the effect of Committee Formation.
    1. The owner of Committee Formation may play riders before they resolve Committee Formation.
  2. The Confusing Legal Text and Confounding Legal Text action cards may be played after Committee Formation has been discarded to change who the elected player is, which will negate the effects of Committee Formation.
    1. The Deadly Plot action card may be played after Committee Formation has been discarded to discard the agenda without resolving it, but only if that player predicted a different outcome from some other game effect.

sections.title: Compensated Disarmament
sections.html:
1. All trade goods are gained together.
  2. Each destroyed infantry will provide one trade good and each destroyed mech will provide one trade good.
  3. A planet with zero units on it is eligible to be elected.
  4. Structures are unaffected by Compensated Disarmament.
    1. The Titans of Ul’s Hel–Titans are also ground forces and are thus affected by Compensated Disarmament.

sections.title: Conventions of War
sections.html: 1. When Conventions of War is a law in play a player may still use the Tactical Bombardment action card, the X–89 Bacterial Weapon technology or the Stellar Converter relic on a cultural planet.

sections.title: Core Mining
sections.html: 1. A planet with zero infantry on it may be elected.

sections.title: Covert Legislation
sections.html:
1. If the Speaker draws Classified Document Leaks, Judicial Abolishment, Miscount Disclosed or New Constitution, when that agenda would be discarded if revealed, both the hidden agenda and Covert Legislation are discarded.
  2. Any effects that take place when or after an agenda is revealed instead take place when or after the speaker has drawn and announced the possible outcomes for the hidden agenda.
  3. If an effect, such as the Veto action card, would discard Covert Legislation, both it and the hidden agenda are discarded.
  4. The hidden agenda is only revealed as it is resolved. All abilities that may be played after voting, such as the Bribery, Confounding Legal Text, Confusing Legal Text or Deadly Plot action cards, must be played before the agenda is revealed.
  5. The speaker may still vote on Covert Legislation.

sections.title: The Crown of Emphidia
sections.html:
1. If The Crown of Emphidia law is discarded, no player loses a victory point.
  2. If the player that gains The Crown of Emphidia controls no planets in their home system, they cannot lose it.

sections.title: Economic Equality
sections.html: 1. If the “For” outcome of Economic Equality is resolved, the Mentak player may resolve their Pillage faction ability against each of their neighbors.

sections.title: Enforced Travel Ban
sections.html:
1. The effect of the Enforced Travel Ban law does not affect the Creuss player.
  2. Enforced Travel Ban only prevents movement using the normal adjacency provided by wormholes. Other effects that create adjacency, such as the Wormhole Reconstruction agenda or the Lost Star Chart action card, may be used to allow movement between systems containing wormholes.
  3. When the Enforced Travel Ban law is in play, units cannot move through wormholes, even by effects that move ships outside of the Movement step of a tactical action, such as while retreating.
  4. When the Enforced Travel Ban law is in play, hits may still be produced against ships in the active system by units with the Deep Space Cannon ability in systems that are adjacent via a wormhole during the Space Cannon Offense step of a tactical action.
  5. Players may still be neighbors via systems that are adjacent via wormholes.
  6. The “Against” effect of Enforced Travel Ban will affect PDS in or adjacent to systems containing an alpha, beta, delta or gamma wormhole.

sections.title: Executive Sanctions
sections.html: 1. The effect of the Executive Sanctions law does not affect the Yssaril player.

sections.title: Fleet Regulations
sections.html:
1. The effect of the Fleet Regulations law does not prevent the Letnev player from using their Armada faction ability. They may have up to six non–fighter ships in a system if they have four command tokens in their fleet pool.
  2. The Mahact player may only have up to four command tokens in their fleet pool when the Fleet Regulations law is in play, regardless of which faction the command tokens belong to.

sections.title: Galactic Crisis Pact
sections.html:
1. Players resolve the secondary ability of the elected strategy card in speaker order.
  2. The secondary ability is resolved immediately, during the agenda phase.
  3. Players must pay the influence or resource costs to resolve the abilities of the Leadership, Warfare or Technology strategy cards if they are elected. Any planets used to pay these costs will ready at the end of the agenda phase.
  4. If the Technology strategy card is elected, a player may exhaust a planet with a technology specialty to ignore a prerequisite on a technology as normal. This planet will ready at the end of the agenda phase.
    1. A player may exhaust the AI Development Algorithm technology to ignore a prerequisite on a unit upgrade technology as normal. AI Development Algorithm will not ready at the end of the agenda phase.
  5. If a player has a strategy card in their play area due to the effect of the Political Stability action card, that strategy card is eligible to be elected.

sections.title: Holy Planet of Ixth
sections.html: 1. If the Holy Planet of Ixth law is discarded, no player loses a victory point.

sections.title: Homeland Defense Act
sections.html: 1. If the Homeland Defense Act law is discarded, players might have to remove PDS so that they have no more than two on each planet.

sections.title: Imperial Arbiter
sections.html:
1. If either strategy card had trade goods on it at the start of the strategy phase, those trade goods remain with the player that originally chose the strategy card.
  2. In a three– or four–player game, the owner of Imperial Arbiter chooses which strategy cards are swapped.

sections.title: Ixthian Artifact
sections.html:
1. A player must still meet the prerequisites for the technology they research.
    1. A player may use the first technology they research to meet the prerequisites of the second technology they research.
    2. A player may exhaust a planet with a technology specialty to ignore a prerequisite on a technology as normal. This planet will ready at the end of the agenda phase.
    3. A player may exhaust the AI Development Algorithm technology to ignore a prerequisite on a unit upgrade technology as normal. AI Development Algorithm will not ready at the end of the agenda phase.
  2. A player with three or fewer units in a system adjacent to the Mecatol Rex system destroys all of their units in that system. Otherwise, a player chooses which three units are destroyed.
  3. All units are destroyed simultaneously.
  4. To cast votes against or to play a rider on Ixthian Artifact is to commit heresy.

sections.title: Judicial Abolishment
sections.html:
1. If Judicial Abolishment is revealed when only one law is in play, players may only vote for that law or abstain. If no votes are cast, the speaker must decide for that law to be elected.
    1. Players may still play riders if only one law is in play.

sections.title: Minister of Commerce
sections.html:
1. Minister of Commerce triggers when its owner has their commodities replenished by any game effect.
    1. Gaining a fixed number of commodities does not trigger Minister of Commerce, even if doing so would result in its owner having commodities equal to their commodity value.
  2. All trade goods are gained together.

sections.title: Minister of Exploration
sections.html: 1. If the owner of Minister of Exploration gains control of multiple planets during one invasion, the trade goods are gained one at a time.

sections.title: Minister of Industry
sections.html:
1. All units in that system may use their Production ability, not just the placed space dock.
  2. The produced units must be paid for.
  3. A space dock cannot be placed on a planet already containing a space dock.
    1. If a player has no space docks in their reinforcements when they may place a space dock on they game board, they may first remove a space dock from a system that does not contain their command token. However, they cannot then place the space dock on the same planet that they removed it from.
  4. An ability that puts a space dock on the game board by “replacing”, rather than “placing”, such as the Infiltrate action card, will trigger Minister of Industry.

sections.title: Minister of Peace
sections.html:
1. Once a player resolves the ability of Minister of Peace, the active player cannot use any “after you activate a system” abilities.
    1. Other players, including the Minister of Peace player, cannot use any “after another player activates a system that…” abilities.
  2. The active player may still use any “at the end of your turn” abilities when their turn is ended by Minister of Peace.
  3. The player that owns Minister of Peace does not have to have any of their units in the active system to resolve Minister of Peace, so long as any non–active player owns at least one unit in the active system.

sections.title: Minister of Policy
sections.html:
1. The owner of Minister of Policy will draw action cards during the Draw Action Cards step of the status phase, and again at the end of the status phase.
    1. If the Yssaril player owns Minister of Policy, they will use their Scheming ability for both the Draw Action Cards step and for Minister of Policy. However, they do not draw all the cards together; they must fully resolve Scheming by discarding an action card for the Draw Action Cards step before drawing any action cards for Minister of Policy.
  2. Neural Motivator does not apply when the owner of Minister of Policy draws action cards from its effect.

sections.title: Minister of War
sections.html: 1. Effects that trigger at the start or end of a player’s turn will not trigger between each of those player’s action.

sections.title: Miscount Disclosed
sections.html:
1. If Miscount Disclosed is revealed when only one law is in play, players may only vote for that law or abstain. If no votes are cast, the speaker must decide for that law to be elected.
    1. Players may still play riders if only one law is in play.
  2. The elected law remains in play, and remains elected to the same object if applicable, while it is being voted on.
    1. If Articles of War is elected by Miscount Disclosed, the Hacan player’s transactions during the revote cannot involve any planets containing their Pride of Kenara mechs, and the Empyrean player cannot cancel action cards played during the revote with their Watcher mechs.
    2. If Classified Document Leaks is elected by Miscount Disclosed, the objective that was originally elected will remain a public objective during the vote. It therefore cannot be re–elected.
    3. If Committee Formation is elected by Miscount Disclosed, the owner may use its ability. The elected player will receive Committee Formation from the discard pile.
    4. If Homeland Defense Act is elected by Miscount Disclosed, and the “For” effect is resolved again, players will not have to remove any PDS from the board.
    5. If Political Censure is elected by Miscount Disclosed, the current owner cannot play action cards, including Confounding Legal Text, if another player is elected. If another player is elected, that player may play the Confusing Legal Text action card.
    6. If Wormhole Reconstruction is elected by Miscount Disclosed, the Mentak player will remain neighbors with players through wormholes, allowing them to use their Pillage faction ability on those players. The Empyrean player’s Watcher mechs will remain adjacent to other players’ units through wormholes, allowing them to cancel action cards played with the mech’s ability.
    7. If Representative Government is elected by Miscount Disclosed, each player will cast only one vote during the revote.
    8. If the elected law is attached to a planet, and is increasing its influence value, the player that controls that planet may still cast votes using the increased influence.
  3. Once the law is elected, any riders on Miscount Disclosed will resolve. Following that, the elected law is then treated as being revealed.
    1. If Classified Document Leaks is elected by Miscount Disclosed, and there are no other secret objectives eligable to be elected by the Miscount Disclosed revote, Classified Document Leaks will be discarded and replaced.
    2. When the elected law is treated as revealed, the Veto action card, the Xxcha Quash faction ability, or the Xxcha Political Favor promissory note may be played. If so, the law will be discarded and replaced.
    3. The Political Secret promissory note may also be played when the elected law is treated as revealed.
    4. After the elected law is treated as revealed, riders may be played to predict the outcome of the elected law.
  4. After all players have voted for Miscount Disclosed, the Deadly Plot action card may be played. If so, the elected law is not voted on and remains in play.
  5. After all players have voted for the elected law, the Deadly Plot action card may be played. If so, the elected law is discarded.
  6. Players who resolved a transaction while voting on and resolving Miscount Disclosed may resolve an additional transaction voting on and resolving the elected law.
  7. If Holy Planet of Ixth, Shard of the Throne or The Crown of Emphidia is elected by Miscount Disclosed, the owner will not lose a victory point.

sections.title: Mutiny
sections.html: 1. If the “For” outcome of Mutiny is resolved, players gain victory points in speaker order.

sections.title: New Constitution
sections.html: 1. If a player controls planets in another player’s home system, those planets are not exhausted by the “For” outcome of New Constitution.

sections.title: Nexus Sovereignty
sections.html:
1. The effect of the Nexus Sovereignty law does not affect the Creuss player.
  2. When the Nexus Sovereignty law is in play, units cannot move through the alpha and beta wormholes in the wormhole nexus, even by effects that move ships outside of the movement step of a tactical action, such as while retreating.
  3. When the Nexus Sovereignty law is in play, hits may still be produced against ships in the active system by units with the Deep Space Cannon ability in systems that are adjacent via a wormhole during the Space Cannon Offense step of a tactical action.
  4. Players may still be neighbors via systems that are adjacent via wormholes.

sections.title: Political Censure
sections.html: 1. When a player is elected for Political Censure, they may play the Confusing Legal Text or Deadly Plot action cards before it resolves.

sections.title: Prophecy of Ixth
sections.html: 1. Other effects that produce units without a unit using its Production ability will not cause Prophecy of Ixth to be discarded.

sections.title: Publicize Weapon Schematics
sections.html:
1. If the Publicize Weapon Schematics law is in play, and a player is the first to gain the war sun unit upgrade technology, from then on, prerequisites for the war sun unit upgrade technology will be ignored.
  2. If the Muaat does not own their Prototype War Sun II faction unit upgrade technology, they do not own a war sun technology.
    1. If the Publicize Weapon Schematics law is in play, the Muaat player will not cause prerequisites for the War Sun unit upgrade technology to be ignored if they do not own their Prototype War Sun II faction unit upgrade technology.
    2. If the “Against” outcome of Publicize Weapon Schematics is resolved, the Muaat player will not discard their action cards if they do not own their Prototype War Sun II faction unit upgrade technology.
  3. The Muaat player’s Prototype War Sun will lose its Sustain Damage ability, regardless of if the Muaat player owns their Prototype War Sun II faction unit upgrade technology.

sections.title: Rearmament Agreement
sections.html:
1. A player that controls no planets in their home system will not place a mech if the “For” outcome of Rearmament Agreement is resolved.
  2. If a player wishes to place a mech, but there are none in their reinforcements, they may remove a mech from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. The mech will be placed undamaged.
  3. A player that has no mechs on the game board is unaffected by the “Against” effect of Rearmament Agreement.

sections.title: Research Grant Reallocation
sections.html:
1. A player may gain any technology, regardless of the number of command tokens in their fleet pool.
    1. If a player must remove more command tokens than they have in their fleet pool, they remove all their command tokens from their fleet pool instead.
  2. The number and colors of technologies a player owns will have no effect on the number of command tokens they remove.
    1. A player cannot exhaust a planet with a technology specialty to reduce the number of command tokens they remove.

sections.title: Research Team: Biotic
sections.html: 1. The agenda card, not the planet, is exhausted to ignore the prerequisite.

sections.title: Research Team: Cybernetic
sections.html: 1. The agenda card, not the planet, is exhausted to ignore the prerequisite.

sections.title: Research Team: Propulsion
sections.html: 1. The agenda card, not the planet, is exhausted to ignore the prerequisite.

sections.title: Research Team: Warfare
sections.html: 1. The agenda card, not the planet, is exhausted to ignore the prerequisite.

sections.title: Search Warrant
sections.html:
1. A player with three scored secret objectives may draw a fourth. However, they must immediately shuffle it into the secret objective deck.
  2. If the elected player has three secret objective cards, and they would draw another, the drawn secret objective card is revealed before that player chooses which card to discard. This applies both when the elected player initially draws the secret objective cards from the effect of Search Warrant when they are elected, and if they later draw secret objective cards from another effect.
  3. If a player draws the Drive the Debate secret objective while resolving Search Warrant, they cannot score it immediately.

sections.title: Seed of an Empire
sections.html: 1. If multiple players have the most or fewest victory points, they gain victory points in speaker order.

sections.title: Shard of the Throne
sections.html: 1. If the Shard of the Throne law is discarded, no player loses a victory point.

sections.title: Shared Research
sections.html:
1. If the Shared Research law is in play, a player still cannot move into a nebula unless it is the active system.
  2. If the Shared Research law is in play, a ship that begins the Movement step of a tactical action in a nebula still treats its move value as one for the duration of that step.

sections.title: Swords to Plowshares
sections.html: 1. Mechs are ignored by the “For” effect of Swords to Plowshares.

sections.title: Wormhole Reconstruction
sections.html:
1. While Wormhole Reconstruction is in play, Enforced Travel Ban will have no effect.
  2. The “Against” effect of Wormhole Reconstruction will cause each player to place command tokens in each system that contains an alpha, beta, delta or gamma wormhole and one or more of that player’s ships.

sections.title: Wormhole Research
sections.html:
1. A player with ships in a delta or gamma wormhole may research a technology from the “For” effect. Those ships will not be destroyed.
    1. If a system contains both a delta and gamma wormhole and an alpha or beta wormhole, such as the active wormhole nexus, then ships in that system will be destroyed.
  2. A player must still meet the prerequisites for the technology they research.
    1. A player may exhaust a planet with a technology specialty to ignore a prerequisite on a technology as normal. This planet will ready at the end of the agenda phase.
    2. A player may exhaust the AI Development Algorithm technology to ignore a prerequisite on a unit upgrade technology as normal. AI Development Algorithm will not ready at the end of the agenda phase.
  3. Ground forces in the space area of a system containing an alpha or beta wormhole will be removed due to lack of capacity after the ships in that system are destroyed; those ground forces will not trigger any “destroyed” effects. Fighters will be destroyed, and will trigger any “destroyed” effects.
  4. If Anti–Intellectual Revolution is in play as a law, players who research a technology will destroy a ship due to Anti–Intellectual Revolution before they destroy ships in systems containing alpha or beta wormholes. As such, they may choose a ship in a system containing an alpha or beta wormhole to destroy for Anti–Intellectual Revolution
    1. If the Vuil’raith player has their flagship, The Terror Between, in a system containing an alpha or beta wormhole, and they choose to destroy it for Anti–Intellectual Revolution, then they will not capture the other ships in that system that are destroyed by Wormhole Research.
    2. If the Vuil’raith player has their flagship, The Terror Between, in a system containing an alpha or beta wormhole, and they choose to destroy another ship with capacity, they must resolve capacity before Wormhole Research destroys any ships. Any fighters they remove due to capacity will not be captured when ships are destroyed for Wormhole Research.
  5. The Saar player’s Floating Factories will not be destroyed by Wormhole Research.

sections.title: Age of Commerce
sections.html:
1. Players must still be neighbors on the game board for the purpose of resolving game effects that depend on players being neighbors.
    1. For example, the Mentak player must still be neighbors with another player on the game board to resolve their Pillage faction ability against that player.
  2. The Hacan player’s Guild Ships faction ability and Trade Convoys promissory note provide no benefit while playing with the Age of Commerce event. However, Trade Convoys may still be played as a component action.
  3. If the Empyrean player receives commodities from a player with their Dark Pact promissory note in their play area equal to that player’s printed commodity value, then both players will gain one trade good. This need not be all of the giving player’s current commodities.
    1. If the giving player owns the Dynamis Core relic, they must give two commodities above their faction’s printed commodity value to trigger the effect of Dark Pact.
  4. When a player’s Trade Agreement promissory note is played, they give only the number of commodities that they just gained due to replenishing commodities.
  5. A player may share any number of technologies in a single transaction.

sections.title: Age of Exploration
sections.html:
1. If there are no more blue–backed or red–backed tiles available, a player does not place any tile if they roll the corresponding dice result.
  2. The Dark Energy Tap technology retains all its printed abilities when it is exhausted.
  3. New tiles cannot be placed adjacent to the Creuss or Rebellion home systems, the wormhole nexus, or systems that comprise The Fracture.

sections.title: Age of Fighters
sections.html: 1. The Vuil’raith player still captures ships that they destroy via their various abilities. These ships are purged when they would be returned to their original owner.

sections.title: Cosmic Phenomanae
sections.html:
1. Only ships moving out of gravity rifts may apply the +2 to their move value; ships moving through cannot.
  2. For ships moving out of a gravity rift, the active player chooses for each one whether it applies +1 or +2 to its move value, and then rolls for removing with the corresponding threshold.
  3. Ships that move out of a gravity rift outside of the movement step of a tactical action, such as through retreating from a space combat, must still roll for removal. Their owner may choose which threshold to use.

sections.title: Dangerous Wilds
sections.html: 1. The player may research the technology before or after they explore the planet.

sections.title: Minor Factions
sections.html:
1. During setup, if a player places a minor faction system with two planets, that player chooses which planet gets two neutral infantry and which planet gets one.
  2. During setup, if a player is dealt the Creuss reference card, they place the Creuss Gate (tile 17) in the equidistant, and place the Creuss home system (tile 51) in the common play area.
  3. During setup, if a player is dealt the Rebellion reference card, they place the Sorrow (tile 94) in the equidistant, and place the Rebellion home system (tile 118) in the common play area.
  4. During setup, if a player is dealt the Keleres reference card, then they select a home system at random from amongst the Argent, Mentak and Xxcha, excluding any that have already been placed.
    1. Should another player have the reference card for that faction, then they take that home system, and the player with the Keleres reference card places a different home system at random.
    2. The pool of player factions and minor factions cannot contain all four of the Argent, Keleres, Mentak and Xxcha.
    3. When a player controls each planet in this system, they take the Keleres alliance card, granting them the ability of Suffi An, the Keleres commander. They are not granted the ability of the Argent, Mentak or Xxcha commanders.
  5. If Mahact exists as a minor faction, the player that controls Ixth gains access to the ability of Il Na Viroset, the Mahact commander.
  6. Commander abilities of minor factions do not need to be unlocked; they are available as soon as a player takes the corresponding alliance card.
  7. When a player gains control of a minor faction planet, if it is not controlled by another player, they explore it. They choose which planet trait they explore it as.
  8. A player only loses a minor faction’s alliance card if a single other player controls each planet in that minor faction’s system.
    1. A player will retain a minor faction’s alliance card even if they control no planets in that minor faction’s system, should two or more other players each control planets in that system.
  9. The planets in a minor faction’s system are not home planets, nor is the system a home system.
    1. The minor faction systems cannot be used to score objectives such as Conquer the Weak or Darken the Skies, but may be used to score objectives such as Expand Borders.
    2. The minor faction systems may be targeted by action cards such as Reactor Meltdown, Signal Jamming or Uprising.
    3. The minor faction systems may be elected for agendas such as Colonial Redistribution. They will be unaffected by agendas such as New Constitution or Shared Research.
    4. The minor faction systems may be targeted with the Stellar Converter relic or with the Muaat player’s Nova Seed hero ability. These will not cause a player to lose an alliance card.
  10. All neutral infantry have a combat value of 8, and otherwise have no special abilities, regardless of which minor faction they belong to.
  11. Minor factions are not players.
    1. Planets with neutral infantry cannot be targeted with action cards such as Plague or Uprising.
    2. Planets with neutral infantry cannot be elected by “elect planet” agendas, and are unaffected by agendas such as Swords to Plowshares.
    3. Planets with neutral infantry cannot be used to score objectives such as Make an Example of their World or Stake Your Claim.

sections.title: Monuments to the Ages
sections.html:
1. If a player would gain their final victory point at the start of the status phase from a monument, they immediately win the game. Players will not score objectives.
    1. If multiple players would gain their final victory simultaneously, the player with the lowest initiative wins.
    2. All commodities are placed with monuments simultaneously. A player with two monuments and a lower initiative may gain multiple points and win.

sections.title: Rapid Mobilization
sections.html: 1. During setup, if a player gains and readies a planet with a technology specialty, they may exhaust that planet when they research a technology to ignore a prerequisite.

sections.title: Stellar Atomics
sections.html:
1. If all players have removed their control token from Stellar Atomics, then no player will vote on agendas, and the speaker will decide which outcome is resolved.
  2. Players may still resolve non–action card abilities during the action phase.
  3. If the Xxcha player has Elder Qanoj, their commander, unlocked, they will be able to vote after removing their control token from Stellar Atomics.

sections.title: Total War
sections.html:
1. Commodities on planets are not treated as commodities for any game effect, other than those that appear on the Total War event card.
    1. The Mentak player cannot use their Pillage faction ability to target the commodities on planets.
    2. The Salvage action card cannot be used to target the commodities on planets.
  2. If a player gains control of a planet in another player’s home system, without controlling at least one planet in their own home system, then any commodities on the planet they gained control of remain on that planet.
    1. The commodities on the planet in the other player’s home system cannot be discarded to gain a victory point.
    2. If that player still controls that planet in another player’s home system when they regain control of a planet in their own home system, they then move the commodities from the planet in the other player’s home system to the planet in their own home system.

sections.title: Wild, Wild Galaxy
sections.html:
1. A player with no planets remaining in their home system is not prevented from scoring public objectives.
  2. If the Muaat player’s Nova Seed hero ability replaces a player’s home system with a supernova, then that supernova becomes that player’s home system.

sections.title: Abandoned Warehouses
sections.html: 1. A player cannot have more commodities than their commodity value.

sections.title: Cultural Relic Fragment
sections.html:
1. If the relic deck is empty, a player may still purge three Cultural Relic Fragments as an action.
  2. If an eliminated player had any Cultural Relic Fragments, they are discarded to the cultural planet exploration discard pile.

sections.title: Dead World
sections.html: 1. If the relic deck is empty, Dead World will be discarded with no effect.

sections.title: Demilitarized Zone
sections.html: 1. After the active player has returned ground forces on the planet to the space area, if they do not have enough capacity in the space area for the returned ground forces, including zero capacity, they will have to remove fighters and/or ground forces to meet capacity limits.

sections.title: Derelict Vessel
sections.html: 1. A player with three scored secret objectives may draw a fourth. However, they must immediately shuffle it into the secret objective deck.

sections.title: Enigmatic Device
sections.html: 1. A player cannot play Enigmatic Device as a component action if they have less than six resources available.

sections.title: Freelancers
sections.html:
1. A planet may be exhausted to spend its influence or resources, but not both.
  2. If a player is to gain multiple planets in a system, they choose the order in which they gain them, and explore each planet as they gain it before gaining the next. As such, a player cannot place ground forces produced by Freelancers on a planet in the active system that they are yet to gain and explore.
  3. If a player wishes to place a unit, but there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, they may remove a unit of that type from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. This unit will be placed undamaged.

sections.title: Functioning Base
sections.html: 1. A player cannot have more commodities than their commodity value.

sections.title: Hazardous Relic Fragment
sections.html:
1. If the relic deck is empty, a player may still purge three Hazardous Relic Fragments as an action.
  2. If an eliminated player had any Hazardous Relic Fragments, they are discarded to the hazardous planet exploration discard pile.

sections.title: Industrial Relic Fragment
sections.html:
1. If the relic deck is empty, a player may still purge three Industrial Relic Fragments as an action.
  2. If an eliminated player had any Industrial Relic Fragments, they are discarded to the industrial planet exploration discard pile.

sections.title: Ion Storm
sections.html:
1. The active player chooses which side of the Ion Storm token is initially face up.
  2. All ship movement is simultaneous. If the Ion Storm token system is the active system, and the token is currently on the alpha side, a player cannot move a ship from a system with an alpha wormhole, flip the token, then move a ship from a system with the beta wormhole (then flip the token again).
    1. The Creuss player may do this by moving their Hil Colish flagship before or after their other ships.
  3. If the Ion Storm token is in a system containing a wormhole of the same type, a player chooses which wormhole they use when moving through a wormhole of that type. The Ion Storm token only flips if it was the chosen wormhole.
    1. As a system is never adjacent to itself, a ship cannot move out through one wormhole and in through the other while remaining in the system. The ship must pass through another system with a wormhole to use both wormholes.
  4. If ships are moved through the Ion Storm token wormhole outside of the Move Ship or Retreat substeps of a tactical action, such as by the effect of the Skilled Retreat action card, the Ion Storm token is not flipped.

sections.title: Local Fabricators
sections.html:
1. A player cannot have more commodities than their commodity value.
  2. If a player wishes to place a mech, but there are none left in their reinforcements, they may remove a mech from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. The mech will be placed undamaged.

sections.title: Unknown Relic Fragment
sections.html:
1. A player cannot purge three Unknown Relic Fragments to gain a relic. At least one cultural, hazardous or industrial relic fragment must be purged.
  2. If an eliminated player had any Unknown Relic Fragments, they are discarded to the frontier exploration discard pile.

sections.title: The Acropolis — Emelpar
sections.html: 1. The owner of The Acropolis may ready a component in another player’s play area.

sections.title: The Atrament — Primor
sections.html: 1. Both infantry must be placed on the same planet.

sections.title: Dok ’N Pic’s Salvage Yard — Garbozia
sections.html:
1. Cards on Dok ’N Pic’s Salvage Yard do not count towards a player’s action card hand limit.
  2. The player with The Codex cannot take cards that are on Dok ’N Pic’s Salvage Yard.
