  3. If another player gains control of Garbozia, any action cards on Dok ’N Pic’s Salvage Yard will remain there when the legendary planet ability card is transferred; the new controller of Garbozia may play those action cards in the future.
  4. Dok ’N Pic’s Salvage Yard need not be readied for a player to play the action cards on it.

sections.title: The Galactic Council — Mecatol Rex
sections.html:
1. The Galactic Council cannot be exhausted by a player that has no unscored secret objective cards in their hand.
  2. When using The Galactic Council, the active player first discards a secret objective, shuffling it into the secret objective deck. Then, they draw a secret objective. This may result in them drawing the secret objective they discarded.

sections.title: Maxis Central Control — Faunus
sections.html: 1. If the gained planet was not controlled by another player, it is explored.

sections.title: Achieve Supremacy
sections.html: 1. The flagship or war sun may be in the home system of an eliminated player.

sections.title: Adapt New Strategies
sections.html: 1. A Valefar Assimilator technology will count if it is currently copying another player’s faction technology.

sections.title: Amass Wealth
sections.html:
1. The influence, resources and trade goods must be spent during the status phase. Any that were spent during the action phase will have no effect.
  2. A planet may be exhausted to spend either its resource or influence value, but not both.
  3. Trade goods may be spent as influence or resources when scoring Amass Wealth.

sections.title: Become a Legend
sections.html:
1. The number of units in the system is irrelevant, if there is at least one.
  2. A ship, ground force, or structure will all qualify for Become a Legend.
    1. If one player has a ground force or structure on a planet in a qualifying system, and another player has a ship in the same system, both players may count the system towards the requirements of Become a Legend.
    2. A player may have ships in the system containing a legendary planet or Mecatol Rex without controlling the planet for that system to count towards the requirements of Become a Legend.
  3. If Mirage is placed in an anomaly, or the Nano–Forge relic is attached to a planet in an anomaly, that system will only count as one system towards the requirements of Become a Legend.
  4. Any system containing a Vuil’raith player’s Dimensional Tear is a gravity rift, and thus, an anomaly.
    1. If a Vuil’raith player’s Dimensional Tear is in a system containing another anomaly, a legendary planet, or Mecatol Rex, that system will only count as one system towards the requirements of Become a Legend.

sections.title: Become a Martyr
sections.html:
1. The lost planet may be in any player’s home system. It does not have to be a planet in the home system of the player scoring Become a Martyr.
    1. The lost planet may be in the home system of an eliminated player.
  2. If the lost planet is the last planet a player controls, that player will be eliminated before they score Become a Martyr, if they meet the other requirements for elimination.
  3. If the player with the Shard of the Throne relic loses their home system, they will lose the Shard of the Throne card and the associated victory point before they may score Become a Martyr.
  4. The attacker will have the opportunity to score a secret objective before the defender has the opportunity to score Become a Martyr.

sections.title: Become the Gatekeeper
sections.html:
1. A player with a ship in the wormhole nexus, or in any other system with both an alpha and beta wormhole, qualifies for Become the Gatekeeper.
  2. Any ground forces or structures are irrelevant.

sections.title: Betray a Friend
sections.html:
1. The following promissory notes qualify for scoring Betray a Friend:
    1. Alliance.
    2. Support for the Throne.
    3. Stymie (Arborec).
    4. Share Knowledge (Deepwrought).
    5. Trade Convoys (Hacan).
    6. Dark Pact (Empyrean).
    7. Blood Pact (Empyrean).
    8. Promise of Protection (Mentak).
    9. Gift of Prescience (Naalu).
    10. Antivirus (Nekro).
    11. Sever (Rebellion).
    12. Terraform (Ul).
  2. The defender cannot score Betray a Friend.

sections.title: Brave the Void
sections.html:
1. Any system containing a Vuil’raith player’s Dimensional Tear is a gravity rift, and thus, an anomaly.
  2. A wormhole is not an anomaly.

sections.title: Centralize Galactic Trade
sections.html: 1. The trade goods must be spent during the status phase. Any trade goods that were spent during the action phase will have no effect.

sections.title: Conquer the Weak
sections.html: 1. The planet may be in the home system of an eliminated player.

sections.title: Control the Borderlands
sections.html:
1. The number of units in the system is irrelevant, if there is at least one.
  2. A ship, ground force, or structure will all qualify for Control the Borderlands.
    1. If one player has a ground force or structure on a planet in a qualifying system, and another player has a ship in the same system, both players may count the system towards the requirements of Control the Borderlands.
  3. The units may be in another player’s home system.
  4. The Creuss Gate is not a home system.
  5. The Wormhole Nexus and the Creuss home system are both on the edge of the game board.
  6. If the edge of a system tile is touching a hyperlane tile, that edge does not cause that system tile to be on the edge of the game board.
    1. When using the five– and seven–player hyperlane setups, the system tile in the center of the ring of hyperlanes is not on the edge of the game board.
    2. When using the seven– and eight–player alternate setups, only the system tiles designated as “Ring 3”, and home systems are on the edge of the game board, along with the Creuss home system and the wormhole nexus.

sections.title: Control the Region
sections.html: 1. Any ground forces or structures are irrelevant.

sections.title: Darken the Skies
sections.html: 1. Darken the Skies may be scored by winning a combat in an eliminated player’s home system.

sections.title: Defy Space and Time
sections.html:
1. The number of units in the system is irrelevant, if there is at least one.
  2. A ship, ground force, or structure will all qualify for Defy Space and Time.
    1. If one player has a ground force or structure on Mallice, and another player has a ship in the wormhole nexus, both players may score Defy Space and Time, if it is elected by the Classified Document Leaks agenda.

sections.title: Demonstrate Your Power
sections.html:
1. A player need not win the combat to score Demonstrate Your Power; they are able to score it if their opponent plays the Skilled Retreat action card.
  2. A player involved in a combat due to the Mahact player’s Benediction hero ability may score Demonstrate Your Power after that combat.
  3. Units that are temporarily ships for the duration of a space combat, such as those made so by the Nekro player’s flagship, The Alastor, or the Naaz–Rokha player’s Z–Grav Eidolon mechs, may count towards scoring Demonstrate Your Power.
  4. The Mentak player may use the Sleeper Cell ability of their hero, during the last round of combat to place ships before scoring Demonstrate Your Power. However, fleet pool limits are also checked before scoring.
    1. The Mentak player cannot use the ability of their Salvage Operations technology until after the window in which to score Demonstrate Your Power.

sections.title: Destroy Heretical Works
sections.html:
1. A player will not gain a relic when scoring Destroy Heretical Works.
  2. The relic fragments may be the same or different types.

sections.title: Destroy Their Greatest Ship
sections.html:
1. If a player destroys their own flagship or war sun during combat, such as via the effect of The Crown of Thalnos relic, their opponent cannot score Destroy their Greatest Ship.
  2. Destroy their Greatest Ship is scored as soon as the war sun or flagship is destroyed; it does not require waiting until the end of the combat.
    1. A player does not have to win a combat to score Destroy their Greatest Ship.
  3. A player may score Destroy their Greatest Ship outside of a combat.

sections.title: Develop Weaponry
sections.html:
1. A Valefar Assimilator technology will count if it is currently copying another player’s faction unit upgrade technology.
  2. If the Nekro player owns both a generic unit upgrade technology and a faction unit upgrade technology of the same type, only the faction unit upgrade technology will count for Develop Weaponry.

sections.title: Dictate Policy
sections.html:
1. Dictate Policy is scored after the third law resolves. As such, the Deadly Plot action card will prevent any player from scoring Dictate Policy.
  2. Dictate Policy is scored before any rider action cards are resolved.
  3. If there are three laws in play at the start of the agenda phase, a player may score Dictate Policy immediately.
  4. If the Political Data Nexus Xxcha hero ability puts a third law in play during the action phase, Dictate Policy cannot be scored until the agenda phase.

sections.title: Discover Lost Outposts
sections.html: 1. The number of attachments a planet has is irrelevant, if it has at least one.

sections.title: Drive the Debate
sections.html:
1. Any “For”/“Against” agenda cannot count for Drive the Debate, even if the outcome affects only a single player.
  2. Drive the Debate is scored immediately before the agenda resolves. The Confounding Legal Text and Confusing Legal Text action cards will allow only the newly elected player to score Drive the Debate, and the Deadly Plot action card will prevent any player from scoring Drive the Debate.
  3. Scoring Drive the Debate immediately before the Colonial Redistribution agenda is resolved may change which player(s) can be chosen to place the infantry on the elected planet.
  4. If a player draws Drive the Debate while resolving the Archived Secret or Search Warrant agendas, they cannot score it immediately.

sections.title: Erect a Monument
sections.html:
1. The resources must be spent during the status phase. Any resources that were spent during the action phase will have no effect.
  2. Trade goods may be spent as resources when scoring Erect a Monument.

sections.title: Establish Hegemony
sections.html: 1. With the right attachments, the requirements of Establish Hegemony may be met with a single planet.

sections.title: Expand Borders
sections.html: 1. The planets cannot be in any player’s home system, including those of eliminated players.

sections.title: Explore Deep Space
sections.html:
1. The number of units in the system is irrelevant, if there is at least one.
  2. A system that contains a planet destroyed by the Stellar Converter relic, and no other planets, is considered to contain no planets.

sections.title: Fight with Precision
sections.html:
1. Scoring Fight with Precision will count as that player’s single secret objective scoring for that combat.
  2. Fight with Precision is scored immediately in the Anti–Fighter Barrage step of combat.
    1. A player does not have to win a combat to score Fight with Precision.
  3. If a player’s last fighter in a system is destroyed, but an ability allows that player to then place fighters into that system, Fight with Precision may still be scored.

sections.title: Fight with Precision Ω
sections.html:
1. Scoring Fight with Precision Ω will count as that player’s single secret objective scoring for that combat.
  2. Fight with Precision is scored immediately in the Anti–Fighter Barrage step of combat.
    1. A player does not have to win a combat to score Fight with Precision.
  3. If a player’s last fighter in a system is destroyed, but an ability allows that player to then place fighters into that system, Fight with Precision Ω may still be scored.
  4. Any effect that destroys fighters during the Anti–Fighter Barrage step may be used to score Fight with Precision Ω, not just hits produced by an anti–fighter barrage roll.
    1. For example, say a player plays the Courageous to the End action card when one of their fighters are destroyed during the Anti–Fighter Barrage step. If the dice roll causes their opponent to destroy their ships, and they choose their last fighter, that would allow the player to score Fight with Precision Ω.

sections.title: Form a Spy Network
sections.html: 1. The action cards must be discarded during the status phase. Any action cards that were discarded during the action phase will have no effect.

sections.title: Form Galactic Brain Trust
sections.html: 1. The number of technology specialties a planet has is irrelevant, if it has at least one.

sections.title: Foster Cohesion
sections.html:
1. The Hacan player’s Guild Ships faction ability and Trade Convoys promissory note does not make a player neighbors with all other players.
  2. If a player has units or controls a planet in a system containing an alpha wormhole, and the Creuss player has units or controls a planet in a system containing a beta wormhole, or vice versa, those two players are neighbors.

sections.title: Found a Golden Age
sections.html:
1. The resources must be spent during the status phase. Any resources that were spent during the action phase will have no effect.
  2. Trade goods may be spent as resources when scoring Found a Golden Age.

sections.title: Found Research Outposts
sections.html: 1. The number of technology specialties a planet has is irrelevant, if it has at least one.

sections.title: Galvanize the People
sections.html:
1. The command tokens must be spent during the status phase. Any command tokens that were spent during the action phase will have no effect.
  2. Any effect that triggers when a command token is spent will be triggered six times. For example, if the Muaat player has unlocked their commander, Magmus, they will gain six trade goods, one at a time, when scoring Galvanize the People.

sections.title: Hoard Raw Materials
sections.html: 1. With the right attachments, the requirements of Hoard Raw Materials may be met with a single planet.

sections.title: Hold Vast Reserves
sections.html:
1. The influence, resources and trade goods must be spent during the status phase. Any that were spent during the action phase will have no effect.
  2. A planet may be exhausted to spend either its resource or influence value, but not both.
  3. Trade goods may be spent as influence or resources when scoring Hold Vast Reserves.

sections.title: Improve Infrastructure
sections.html:
1. The number of structures on the planet is irrelevant, if there is at least one.
  2. The structures may be on planets in another player’s home system.
  3. The Saar player’s Floating Factories cannot be used to score Improve Infrastructure.

sections.title: Intimidate Council
sections.html:
1. Any ships in the Mecatol Rex system are irrelevant.
  2. Any ground forces or structures are irrelevant.

sections.title: Lead From the Front
sections.html:
1. The command tokens must be spent during the status phase. Any command tokens that were spent during the action phase will have no effect.
  2. Any effect that triggers when a command token is spent will be triggered three times. For example, if the Muaat player has unlocked their commander, Magmus, they will gain three trade goods, one at a time when scoring Lead From the Front.

sections.title: Learn the Secrets of the Cosmos
sections.html:
1. The three systems may be mutually adjacent to one system, or separate systems.
  2. Having ships in an anomaly is irrelevant, unless that system is also adjacent to another anomaly.
  3. Any ground forces or structures are irrelevant.
  4. Any system containing a Vuil’raith player’s Dimensional Tear is a gravity rift, and thus, an anomaly.

sections.title: Make an Example of Their World
sections.html:
1. If the last ground force is destroyed using the X–89 Bacterial Weapon Ω technology, Make an Example of Their World cannot be scored.
  2. Scoring Make an Example of Their World will not prevent that player from scoring a secret objective in any ground combats during this tactical action.
  3. If a player’s last ground force on a planet is destroyed, but an ability allows that player to then place ground forces onto that planet, Make an Example of Their World may still be scored.
  4. The L1Z1X player may score Make an Example of Their World by using their Harrow faction ability. If they do they cannot score another objective during that ground combat.

sections.title: Make an Example of Their World Ω
sections.html:
1. If the last ground force is destroyed using the X–89 Bacterial Weapon Ω technology, Make an Example of Their World Ω may be scored.
  2. Scoring Make an Example of Their World Ω will not prevent that player from scoring a secret objective in any ground combats during this tactical action.
  3. If a player’s last ground force on a planet is destroyed, but an ability allows that player to then place ground forces onto that planet, Make an Example of Their World Ω may still be scored.
  4. The L1Z1X player cannot score Make an Example of Their World Ω by using their Harrow faction ability.

sections.title: Make History
sections.html:
1. The number of units in the system is irrelevant, if there is at least one.
  2. A ship, ground force, or structure will all qualify for Make History.
    1. If one player has a ground force or structure on a planet in a qualifying system, and another player has a ship in the same system, both players may count the system towards the requirements of Make History.
    2. A player may have ships in the system containing a legendary planet or Mecatol Rex without controlling the planet for that system to count towards the requirements of Make History.
  3. If Mirage is placed in an anomaly, or the Nano–Forge relic is attached to a planet in an anomaly, that system will only count as one system towards the requirements of Make History.
  4. Any system containing a Vuil’raith player’s Dimensional Tear is a gravity rift, and thus, an anomaly.
    1. If a Vuil’raith player’s Dimensional Tear is in a system containing another anomaly, a legendary planet, or Mecatol Rex, that system will only count as one system towards the requirements of Make History.

sections.title: Manipulate Galactic Law
sections.html:
1. The influence must be spent during the status phase. Any influence that was spent during the action phase will have no effect.
  2. Trade goods may be spent as influence when scoring Manipulate Galactic Law.

sections.title: Mechanize the Military
sections.html: 1. Given that each player only has four mechs, to score Mechanize the Military, a player will have to have all of them on the game board, and on separate planets.

sections.title: Negotiate Trade Routes
sections.html: 1. The trade goods must be spent during the status phase. Any trade goods that were spent during the action phase will have no effect.

sections.title: Occupy the Fringe
sections.html: 1. The Saar player’s Floating Factories are never on a planet.

sections.title: Patrol Vast Territories
sections.html:
1. The number of units in the system is irrelevant, if there is at least one.
  2. A system that contains a planet destroyed by the Stellar Converter relic, and no other planets, is considered to contain no planets.

sections.title: Populate the Outer Rim
sections.html:
1. The number of units in the system is irrelevant, if there is at least one.
  2. A ship, ground force, or structure will all qualify for Populate the Outer Rim.
    1. If one player has a ground force or structure on a planet in a qualifying system, and another player has a ship in the same system, both players may count the system towards the requirements of Populate the Outer Rim.
  3. The units may be in another player’s home system.
  4. The Creuss Gate is not a home system.
  5. The Wormhole Nexus and the Creuss home system are both on the edge of the game board.
  6. If the edge of a system tile is touching a hyperlane tile, that edge does not cause that system tile to be on the edge of the game board.
    1. When using the five– and seven–player hyperlane setups, the system tile in the center of the ring of hyperlanes is not on the edge of the game board.
    2. When using the seven– and eight–player alternate setups, only the system tiles designated as “Ring 3” and home systems are on the edge of the game board, along with the Creuss home system and the wormhole nexus.

sections.title: Produce en Masse
sections.html: 1. The number of units in the system is irrelevant, if there is at least one.

sections.title: Protect the Border
sections.html:
1. The number of structures on the planet is irrelevant, if there is at least one.
  2. The structures may be on planets in another player’s home system.
  3. The Saar player’s Floating Factories cannot be used to score Protect the Border.

sections.title: Prove Endurance
sections.html: 1. Prove Endurance is scored when the player passes during the action phase. They may then score another secret objective in the status phase immediately following.

sections.title: Push Boundaries
sections.html: 1. If a player has units or controls a planet in a system containing an alpha wormhole, and the Creuss player has units or controls a planet in a system containing a beta wormhole, or vice versa, those two players are neighbors.

sections.title: Reclaim Ancient Monuments
sections.html: 1. The number of attachments a planet has is irrelevant, if it has at least one.

sections.title: Revolutionize Warfare
sections.html:
1. A Valefar Assimilator technology will count if it is currently copying another player’s faction unit upgrade technology.
  2. If the Nekro player owns both a generic unit upgrade technology and a faction unit upgrade technology of the same type, only the faction unit upgrade technology will count for Revolutionize Warfare.

sections.title: Rule Distant Lands
sections.html:
1. A player will qualify for Rule Distant Lands if they can select two home systems other than their own, and they control a planet in or adjacent to each of those systems.
  2. The planets may meet the criteria by being adjacent to an eliminated player’s home system.
  3. If a player controls a single planet in a home system that is adjacent to another home system via the use of wormholes, that planet alone will not qualify them for Rule Distant Lands.

sections.title: Spark a Rebellion
sections.html:
1. A player that currently outright has the most victory points cannot score Spark a Rebellion.
  2. If multiple players are tied for the most victory points, Spark a Rebellion may be scored by winning a combat against any of them.
    1. Spark a Rebellion may be scored by winning a combat against a player with zero victory points if all players have zero victory points.

sections.title: Strengthen Bonds
sections.html:
1. The following promissory notes qualify for scoring Strengthen Bonds:
    1. Alliance.
    2. Support for the Throne.
    3. Stymie (Arborec).
    4. Share Knowledge (Deepwrought).
    5. Trade Convoys (Hacan).
    6. Dark Pact (Empyrean).
    7. Blood Pact (Empyrean).
    8. Promise of Protection (Mentak).
    9. Gift of Prescience (Naalu).
    10. Antivirus (Nekro).
    11. Sever (Rebellion).
    12. Terraform (Ul).

sections.title: Subdue the Galaxy
sections.html: 1. The planets cannot be in any player’s home system, including those of eliminated players.

sections.title: Sway the Council
sections.html:
1. The influence must be spent during the status phase. Any influence that was spent during the action phase will have no effect.
  2. Trade goods may be spent as influence when scoring Sway the Council.

sections.title: Threaten Enemies
sections.html:
1. Any ships in another players home system are irrelevant.
  2. The ships may be adjacent to the home system of an eliminated player.
  3. Any ground forces or structures are irrelevant.

sections.title: Turn Their Fleets to Dust
sections.html:
1. If the last ship is destroyed using a Direct Hit action card, Turn Their Fleets to Dust cannot be scored.
  2. If a player still has fighters in a system after assigning all hits produced during the Space Cannon Offense step, but is forced to remove all of them to meet capacity limits, Turn Their Fleets to Dust cannot be scored.
  3. If a player’s last ship in a system is destroyed, but an ability allows that player to then place ships into that system, Turn Their Fleets to Dust may still be scored.
  4. Scoring Turn Their Fleets to Dust will not prevent that player from scoring a secret objective in the Space Combat step during this tactical action.

sections.title: Turn Their Fleets to Dust Ω
sections.html:
1. If the last ship is destroyed using a Direct Hit action card, Turn Their Fleets to Dust Ω may be scored.
  2. If a player still has fighters in a system after assigning all hits produced during the Space Cannon Offense step, Turn Their Fleets to Dust Ω may be scored.
  3. If a player’s last ship in a system is destroyed, but an ability allows that player to then place ships into that system, Turn Their Fleets to Dust Ω may still be scored.
  4. Scoring Turn Their Fleets to Dust Ω will not prevent that player from scoring a secret objective in the Space Combat step during this tactical action.
  5. If a system contains only fighters, then Turn Their Fleets to Dust Ω cannot be scored by destroying them.
  6. Any effect that destroys non–fighter ships during the Space Cannon Offense step may be used to score Turn Their Fleets to Dust Ω, not just hits produced by a space cannon roll.
    1. For example, say the Yin player has their flagship, the Van Hauge, destroyed during the Space Cannon Offense step. They may score Turn Their Fleets to Dust Ω if the effect of their flagship destroys all non–fighter ships owned by another player in the active system.

sections.title: Unveil Flagship
sections.html: 1. If a player’s flagship is destroyed during combat, but a later effect places it into the same combat, that player cannot score Unveil Flagship.

sections.title: Alliance
sections.html:
1. An Alliance must be played by the receiving player as soon as it is received. It cannot be kept secret.
    1. If the active player receives an Alliance, they cannot then attempt to trade it with another player. It must be played immediately.
  2. Alliance is returned when the system is activated, even if the active player will perform no hostile acts towards the other player this turn.
  3. If an effect other than activating a system during a tactical action places a command counter in a system with the other player’s units (for example, the primary ability of the Diplomacy strategy card), this will not cause Alliance to be returned.
  4. Activating a system containing only a player’s structures will still cause their Alliance to be returned.
  5. For notes about a commander of a specific faction, see that faction’s notes page.

sections.title: Ceasefire
sections.html:
1. The active player may still use the Space Cannon ability of any units during the Space Cannon Offense step of the tactical action.
  2. If a player has units in the active system from before the tactical action in which their Ceasefire is played, those units will remain in the active system.
  3. If the active player already has units with capacity in the active system, they may transport ground forces on planets in that system into the space area of that system. Those units may then be committed to invade a planet during this tactical action.
  4. If a system containing only a player’s ground forces or structures is activated, that player may still play the active player’s Ceasefire.
  5. Ceasefire does not prevent a player from producing or placing units in the active system.

sections.title: Political Secret
sections.html:
1. A player may still use abilities from their faction technology, leaders, or mechs after their Political Secret has been played.
    1. If a player has had their Political Secret played, other players may still use that player’s other promissory notes.
  2. If an agenda is discarded, each Political Secret that has been played is returned. The affected players may vote on the next agenda as normal.
  3. The effect of Political Secret does not stop a player from using their passive faction ability, only the abilities that player may choose to use.

sections.title: Support For The Throne
sections.html:
1. A Support For The Throne must be played by the receiving player as soon as it is received. It cannot be kept secret.
    1. If the active player receives a Support For The Throne, they cannot then attempt to trade it with another player. It must be played immediately.
  2. Support For The Throne is returned when the system is activated, even if the active player will perform no hostile acts towards the other player this turn.
  3. If an effect other than activating a system during a tactical action places a command counter in a system with the other player’s units (for example, the primary ability of the Diplomacy strategy card), this will not cause Support For The Throne to be returned.
  4. Activating a system containing only a player’s structures will still cause their Support For The Throne to be returned.
  5. If two players trade their Support For The Throne to one another simultaneously, the active player will be the first to gain a victory point.
    1. During the agenda phase, the first player in speaker order will be the first to gain a victory point.

sections.title: Trade Agreement
sections.html:
1. If a player has their maximum number of commodities, and is instructed to replenish their commodities, they will take no commodities. However, that player’s Trade Agreement may be played.
  2. A player does not have to be neighbors with the player that plays their Trade Agreement to give them their commodities.
  3. Trade Agreement cannot be played when a player gains commodities, only when they replenish commodities.

sections.title: Book of Latvinia
sections.html:
1. If a player owns all technologies without prerequisites when they draw the Book of Latvinia, they will not research any technologies.
    1. If a player owns all–but–one technologies without prerequisites when they draw the Book of Latvinia, they will research only that one technology.
  2. A player cannot gain a technology with a prerequisite by ignoring that prerequisite, such as by exhausting a planet with a technology specialty.
  3. If the Nekro player draws the Book of Latvinia, they will gain six command tokens and zero technologies, even if they own all technologies without prerequisites.
  4. When a player uses the component action of the Book of Latvinia, it is purged, regardless of which outcome is resolved.
  5. If a player uses the component action of the Book of Latvinia when they control planets with each type of technology specialty, they mandatorily gain a victory point; they cannot choose instead to gain the speaker token.

sections.title: Circlet of the Void
sections.html:
1. The player that owns Circlet of the Void may move through or into supernovae and/or asteroid fields.
  2. The player that owns Circlet of the Void may move through nebulae, and their ships in nebulae do not have their movement values reduced.
  3. The player that owns Circlet of the Void still applies the movement bonus to their ships that will move through gravity rifts.
  4. The player that owns Circlet of the Void will still ignore anomaly movement effects and not roll for gravity rifts if Circlet of the Void is exhausted.

sections.title: The Codex
sections.html:
1. The action card discard is shuffled to form a new action card deck as soon as the action card deck has zero cards in it.
  2. It is public knowledge which action cards a player takes using The Codex.

sections.title: The Crown of Thalnos
sections.html:
1. A player may only reroll combat rolls with The Crown of Thalnos. They cannot reroll anti–fighter barrage rolls and similar.
  2. If a unit rolls multiple combat dice, it will not be destroyed if it produces at least one hit from its original roll, and that dice is not rerolled, even if it produces no hits from its reroll.
    1. For each unit that rolls multiple combat dice, the player with The Crown of Thalnos should roll those unit’s dice separately from any other combat dice.
  3. A reroll caused by any other effect will not cause a unit to be destroyed.
  4. Units destroyed by The Crown of Thalnos are destroyed at the end of the Roll Dice step, before the Assign Hits step.
  5. A unit with the Sustain Damage ability cannot use it to avoid being destroyed when it fails to produce a hit with the reroll from The Crown of Thalnos.

sections.title: Dynamis Core
sections.html: 1. If a player uses the purge ability of Dynamis Core, they will need to return commodities if they now exceed their original commodity value.

sections.title: Heart of Ixth
sections.html: 1. The “0” side of the d10 represents a result of 10. Heart of Ixth may be used to turn this result into a 9, or vice versa.

sections.title: JR–XS455–O
sections.html:
1. JR–XS455–O is an agent. All rules that apply to agents (and leaders) apply to JR–XS455–O.
    1. JR–XS455–O may be refreshed by the Nomad player's Temporal Command Suite technology.
    2. The ability of JR–XS455–O may be duplicated by the Yssaril player’s agent, Ssruu, if the Yssaril player themselves do not own JR–XS455–O.

sections.title: Lightrail Ordnance
sections.html: 1. The space docks may use the Space Cannon ability during both the Space Cannon Offense and Space Cannon Defense steps.

sections.title: Maw of Worlds
sections.html: 1. The player does not have to meet the prerequisites of the technologies they acquire using Maw of Worlds.

sections.title: Metali Void Shielding
sections.html:
1. The affected ship may be destroyed by the Direct Hit action card after it uses the Sustain Damage ability.
  2. A player may play the Reflective Shielding action card after it uses the Sustain Damage ability via Metali Void Shielding.
  3. If a player owns Metali Void Shielding, and their opponent plays the Waylay action card, they may use Metali Void Shielding for both the Anti–Fighter Barrage and combat rolls in that round of space combat.
  4. Metali Void Shielding has no effect when the Argent player resolves their Raid Formation faction ability.

sections.title: Nano–Forge
sections.html: 1. The attached planet will not have a corresponding legendary planet ability card. However, it will be legendary for effects such as scoring the Make History public objective and similar objectives, transferring the Shard of the Throne relic, and the Winnu player's commander, Rickar Rickani. The attached planet will also no longer be non–legendary for effects such as the Stellar Converter relic.

sections.title: Neuraloop
sections.html:
1. A player may use Neuraloop to purge Neuraloop itself, resolving its ability.
  2. A player may use Neuraloop to purge Nano–Forge, even if it is attached to a planet, if they control that planet. That planet loses the increase to its resources and influence values, and is no longer legendary.
  3. If a player uses Neuraloop to purge another relic that has a purge ability, that purge ability is not resolved.
  4. If a player uses Neuraloop to purge the Circlet of the Void, that player’s units may remain in and move out of any supernovae and/or asteroid fields they are currently in, but cannot move additional units into or through, unless they have another ability that would allow them to do so, such as the Antimass Deflectors technology.
  5. If a player uses Neuraloop to purge the Dynamis Core, and they have more commodities than their faction’s printed commodity value, they return any extras to the supply.
  6. If a player uses Neuraloop to purge The Obsidian, that player must discard one unscored secret objective if they have a total of four scored or unscored secret objectives. There is no effect if they have four scored secret objectives.
  7. If a player uses Neuraloop to purge the Shard of the Throne, that player loses a victory point.
  8. If a player uses Neuraloop to purge another relic, then that player may use Neuraloop again to replace the new objective with yet another objective.
  9. If a player uses Neuraloop to reveal a secret objective as a public objective, that objective does not count towards the limit of three scored or unscored secret objectives for any player that scores it.
  10. A player can score a maximum of one objective of any type during or after each combat. A player cannot score the secret objective revealed by Neuraloop and one of their own secret objectives from the same combat.
  11. A secret objective revealed by Neuraloop becomes a public objective and stops being a secret objective.
  12. The discarded objective is shuffled into its respective deck after the replacement objective is revealed.
    1. This happens before the player with Neuraloop chooses if they wish to purge another relic to replace the new objective. As such, it is possible for the player to reveal the original objective after purging two or more relics.

sections.title: The Prophet’s Tears
sections.html:
1. A player cannot use the ability of The Prophet’s Tears when they directly gain a technology.
  2. The Nekro player may use the ability of The Prophet’s Tears to draw an action card when they would have researched a technology.

sections.title: Scepter of Emelpar
sections.html:
1. If a player has no command tokens in their reinforcements, they must use a command token from their command sheet instead when they use the ability of the Scepter of Emelpar.
  2. The Scepter of Emelpar may be used whenever a command token would be spent from a player’s strategy pool. This includes when spending to perform the secondary ability of a strategy card, for faction abilities, and when scoring objectives.
  3. If the Muaat player uses the ability of the Scepter of Emelpar, they will not gain a trade good from the ability of their commander, Magmus.

sections.title: Shard of the Throne
sections.html:
1. When the player that owns the Shard of the Throne loses control of a legendary planet or a planet in their home system, they immediately give it to the player who gained control of that planet. No abilities may be resolved before this.
  2. If the player that gains Shard of the Throne controls no legendary planets or planets in their home system, they cannot lose it.

sections.title: The Silver Flame
sections.html: 1. The "0" side of the d10 represents a result of 10.

sections.title: Stellar Converter
sections.html:
1. The chosen planet must be in a system adjacent to the unit with bombardment; the planet and unit cannot both be in the same system.
  2. A system that contains a planet destroyed by Stellar Converter, and no other planets, is considered to contain no planets.
  3. A player cannot target a planet they control with Stellar Converter.

sections.title: The Triad
sections.html:
1. The Triad may be readied by effects that ready planets, such as the Diplomacy strategy card.
  2. The Triad is not considered a planet for other game effects.
    1. Units cannot be placed on The Triad.
    2. The Triad cannot be exhausted by the Reparations or Uprising action cards.
    3. The Triad cannot be elected by an “elect planet” agenda, nor can it be exhausted by agenda effects such as the “For” effect of the New Constitution agenda.
    4. Attachments such as the Nano–Forge relic or the Ul Terraform promissory note cannot be attached to The Triad.
    5. The Triad does not count towards the planets required to score the Push Boundaries public objective, nor the Establish Hegemony or Hoard Raw Materials secret objectives. In addition, it does not count towards any objectives that require a planet in a specific type of system.
    6. The Triad does not have a planet trait; it cannot be explored.
    7. The Triad may be exhausted to cast votes, and readies at the end of the agenda phase.

sections.title: Antimass Deflectors
sections.html: 1. The −1 applies to space cannon rolls during both the Space Cannon Offense and Space Cannon Defense steps.

sections.title: Dark Energy Tap
sections.html:
1. A ship may be moved into the system containing the frontier token during the same action that it is explored.
  2. Exploring the frontier token happens at the end of the tactical action. Notably, this is after the Space Cannon Offense and/or Space Combat steps.
  3. Exploring the frontier token is mandatory if the player has a ship in the active system at the end of the tactical action.
  4. When a player gains Dark Energy Tap, they do not immediately explore any frontier tokens in systems containing their ships. They must activate those systems to explore those tokens.
    1. If a player moves or places a ship into a system outside of a tactical action, they cannot explore a frontier token in that system.
  5. The Saar player cannot explore a frontier token with a Floating Factory. However, if they produce a ship during the Production step, they will be able to use that ship to explore the token.
  6. A player cannot use Dark Energy Tap to retreat into a system that contains another player’s units, including ground forces and structures on planets.

sections.title: Sling Relay
sections.html:
1. The produced unit must be paid for.
  2. Sling Relay cannot be used without producing a unit.

sections.title: Fleet Logistics
sections.html:
1. Effects that trigger at the start or end of a player’s turn will not trigger between each of those player’s actions.
  2. A player may use the ability of Fleet Logistics the same turn they gain it.
  3. If a player’s turn is ended by a game effect, they cannot use Fleet Logistics to perform an additional action.
  4. A player cannot use Fleet Logistics to pass on the same turn they performed an action.
  5. If a player’s second action would be to use a component action to play an action card, and that card is cancelled, they are not required to perform an alternate second action on that turn.

sections.title: Neural Motivator
sections.html:
1. Neural Motivator does not apply when a player draws action cards from either of the abilities of the Politics action card, or any other effect outside of the status phase.
  2. Neural Motivator only applies to the Draw Action Card step of the status phase. It does not apply when a player draws action cards due to the effect of the Minister of Policy law or similar effects.

sections.title: Psychoarchaeology
sections.html:
1. When researching a technology, each planet with a technology speciality can only be used to ignore a single prerequisite.
  2. Exhausting planets to gain trade goods can be done at any time during action phase, except when another ability is being resolved. For example, if a player has one of their planets with a technology specialty targeted with the Uprising action card, they cannot use Psychoarchaeology in response to gain a trade good.
  3. If multiple planets are exhausted, the trade goods are gained one at a time.

sections.title: X–89 Bacterial Weapon Ω
sections.html:
1. X–89 Bacterial Weapon Ω may be used against each planet in a system, if the conditions are met.
  2. X–89 Bacterial Weapon Ω will trigger only after all bombardment hits have been assigned.
  3. The L1Z1X may use X–89 Bacterial Weapon Ω after they use their Harrow faction ability.

sections.title: X–89 Bacterial Weapon ΩΩ
sections.html:
1. A player with X–89 Bacterial Weapon ΩΩ must mandatorily double the number of hits they produce.
  2. Effects that cancel hits will only cancel hits based on the doubled number of hits.
  3. Ground forces that are participating in space combat as though they were ships do not double the hits they produce.
    1. Ships that are participating in ground combat as though they were ground forces double the hits they produce.
  4. A player with X–89 Bacterial Weapon ΩΩ must mandatorily exhaust each planet they make a bombardment roll against, even if they produce no hits.
  5. A war sun must target the same planet with all three of its bombardment dice.
    1. If a unit may roll additional bombardment dice, such as by the Plasma Scoring technology, that additional dice must target the same planet.
  6. A player may roll for bombardment against a planet that contains no ground forces.

sections.title: Plasma Scoring
sections.html:
1. Only one additional dice is rolled for each bombardment or space cannon roll, regardless of how many units are using that ability.
    1. During an invasion in a system with multiple planets, only one unit will add a dice to its bombardment roll.
    2. During an invasion, if ground forces have been committed to multiple planets, Plasma Scoring will add an additional dice to the space cannon rolls for each planet during the Space Cannon Defense step.

sections.title: AI Development Algorithm
sections.html:
1. When a player exhausts AI Development Algorithm to ignore a prerequisite of a unit upgrade technology that they are researching, they may still use AI Development Algorithm itself for meeting a warfare technology (red) prerequisite on that unit upgrade technology in the same manner as any other technology.
    1. For example, AI Development Algorithm alone may be used to research the Destroyer II unit upgrade.

sections.title: Magen Defense Grid
sections.html: 1. Magen Defense Grid cannot be used if all of a player’s units in combat that had the Planetary Shield ability have lost it.

sections.title: Magen Defense Grid Ω
sections.html:
1. The player with Magen Defense Grid Ω chooses which ground force the hit is assigned to.
  2. The chosen ground force may cancel the hit by using its Sustain Damage ability, if present. A different ground force with the Sustain Damage ability cannot do so.
  3. If the last of a player’s ground forces in a ground combat are destroyed by the effect of Magen Defense Grid Ω, that player loses the combat immediately. They will be unable to use any “start of combat” abilities.

sections.title: Magen Defense Grid ΩΩ
sections.html:
1. The player with Magen Defense Grid ΩΩ chooses which ground force the hit is assigned to.
  2. The chosen ground force may cancel the hit by using its Sustain Damage ability, if present. A different ground force with the Sustain Damage ability cannot do so.
  3. If the last of a player’s ground forces in a ground combat are destroyed by the effect of Magen Defense Grid ΩΩ, that player loses the combat immediately. They will be unable to use any “start of combat” abilities.
  4. Magen Defense Grid ΩΩ will place infantry regardless of who activates the system.
  5. If a player has multiple structures in the system, one infantry is placed with each.
  6. The infantry must be placed on the same planet as the structure.
    1. If the Saar player owns Magen Defense Grid ΩΩ, and a system containing a Floating Factory is activated, then the infantry will be placed in the space area.

sections.title: Self–Assembly Routines
sections.html:
1. If multiple mechs are destroyed, the trade goods are gained one at a time.
  2. A mech cannot be placed in a space area with Self–Assembly Routines, and so cannot be placed in a system that does not contain a planet.
  3. If a player wishes to place a mech, but there are none left in their reinforcements, they may remove a mech from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. The mech will be placed undamaged.
  4. A player will still gain the trade good for a destroyed mech if Self–Assembly Routines is exhausted.

sections.title: Duranium Armor
sections.html:
1. A player must mandatorily repair a unit with Duranium Armor during each round of combat, if possible.
  2. A player uses Duranium Armor only once during each round of combat, at the end of the Assign Hits substep. Hits assigned outside of this substep will not allow Duranium Armor to repair an additional unit.
  3. Duranium Armor is used even if a player’s opponent produced no hits during a round of combat.
  4. If a player starts a combat with a damaged unit, they use Duranium Armor in the first round of combat.
    1. A player may use Duranium Armor to repair a unit damaged by Space Cannon or Bombardment hits that occurred immediately before the combat.
  5. If a unit is damaged during combat without using its Sustain Damage ability, it may be repaired by Duranium Armor during the same combat round.
  6. Only units participating in the combat may be chosen to be repaired.
  7. Duranium Armor can be used to repair a damaged unit which does not currently have the Sustain Damage ability.

sections.title: Assault Cannon
sections.html:
1. A player with Assault Cannon must mandatorily resolve its ability if they meet the requirement.
  2. If a player loses ships before they can resolve the Assault Cannon ability, they will be unable to resolve it if they no longer have three or more non–fighter ships.
    1. This will most commonly happen when both players in a combat have Assault Cannon, and the defender has exactly three non–fighter ships.
    2. Examples of other abilities that may remove units at the start of a space combat include the Creuss player’s Dimensional Splicer faction technology ability, the Mentak player’s Ambush faction ability, the Yin player’s Impulse Core faction technology ability, as well as abilities such as the Courageous to the End action card or the Reflective Shielding action card that may trigger off of any of the previous abilities.
  3. A player may use an ability to add ships at the start of combat. If this brings the number of non–fighter ships to three or more, the player may then use the ability of Assault Cannon.
    1. Each other player may use one ability after that player has gained ships, and before that player has the opportunity to use the Assault Cannon ability. This may prevent that player from using the ability, as above. 2. Examples of abilities that may add units at the start of space combat include a combination of the Mentak player’s Sleeper Cell hero ability and their Ambush faction ability, the ability of the Nekro player’s flagship, The Alastor, and the Naaz–Rokha player’ Eidolon mech ability.
  4. Effects that cancel hits, such as Sustain Damage, cannot be used to prevent ships from being destroyed.

sections.title: Sarween Tools
sections.html: 1. If units are produced without any unit using its Production ability, Sarween Tools will not provide a reduction to the cost.

sections.title: Scanlink Drone Network
sections.html: 1. The units must be on the planet before the Movement step of the tactical action.

sections.title: Graviton Laser System
sections.html: 1. If multiple players are resolving the Space Cannon ability of their units against the active player, the active player must resolve capacity limits after assigning one player’s hits and before the next player makes their space cannon roll.

sections.title: Predictive Intelligence
sections.html:
1. Neither ability of Predictive Intelligence may be used if it is exhausted.
  2. If a player removes any tokens from their fleet pool, they will need to meet their new fleet pool limits before any other effects may resolve.

sections.title: Transit Diodes
sections.html:
1. When resolving the ability of Transit Diodes, that player may remove ground forces from a system containing their command token.
  2. The ground forces may be removed from on a planet or from in a space area.
  3. The ground forces may be removed from different systems.
  4. The ground forces may be placed on different planets.
  5. If a mech is damaged when it is removed, it will remain damaged when it is placed.

sections.title: Integrated Economy
sections.html:
1. The produced units must be paid for.
  2. There is no limit on the number of units produced, so long as the combined cost does not exceed the planet’s resource value.
  3. Two fighters or two infantry have a combined cost of one resource.
  4. A player may produce ships with Integrated Economy, unless another player has ships in the space area of that planet’s system.

sections.title: War Sun
sections.html:
1. A player without the war sun unit upgrade technology cannot produce, place or have a war sun on the board for any reason.
    1. The Muaat player may do so without owning their Prototype War Sun II faction unit upgrade technology.
  2. If a war sun’s ability results in no units on a planet having the Planetary Shield ability, then the ability of the Magen Defense Grid technology cannot be used during ground combat on that planet.
    1. A war sun has no effect on the Magen Defense Grid Ω or Magen Defense Grid ΩΩ technologies.

sections.title: Flagship
sections.html: 1. For notes about the flagship of a specific faction, see that faction’s notes page.

sections.title: Fighter
sections.html:
1. Fighters and ground forces do not count towards capacity during combat. As such, any number of Fighter II may be in a system during combat, regardless of capacity and fleet pool. This will usually only be caused by effects that place units in a system during combat. When combat ends however, units will need to be removed to meet capacity and fleet pool requirements.
  2. A ship cannot move through a system that contains Fighter II that are controlled by another player during the Movement step of a tactical action.
  3. Ships may be moved into, produced in or placed in a system even if doing so would exceed the fleet pool limit. However, some of those ships must immediately be removed to satisfy the limit. If some of those ships are fighters II, they may instead count towards that player’s capacity in that system. If capacity is exceeded, fighters or ground forces must be removed to meet the limit.

sections.title: Infantry
sections.html:
1. If a player controls no planets in their home system, at the start of their turn, any Infantry II that have been placed on that player’s Infantry II unit upgrade technology card are returned to that player’s reinforcements.
  2. A player need not use one of their twelve plastic infantry units to represent the infantry on their Infantry II unit upgrade card that will be placed in their home system at the start of their next turn, and may use cardboard infantry tokens to represent any and all of these infantry.
